“LEADERS OF 10 BRITISH COMMONWEALTH LANDS 
ACREED TODAY THAT RED CHINA, AS A POTENTIAL NUCLEAR POWER. SHOULD JOIN 
FINAL NEGOTIATIONS FOR A TREATY TO END THE WORLD ARMS RACE. 

AT THE SAME TIME, QUALIFIED INFORMANTS REPORTED THE UNITED STATES 
STANDS READY TO ANNOUNCE TWO IMPORTANT MODIFICATIONS OF ITS PROPOSALS 
FOR A NUCLEAR WEAPONS *TRUCE" WITH RUSSIA. 

ONE MODIFICATION ENVISAGES A BAN ON NUCLEAR WEAPON TESTS LATE IN 
1957 OR EARLY 1958 -- IF RUSSIA AGREES TO NEGOTIATE ARRANGEMENTS TO 
CUT OFF NUCLEAR WEAPON PRODUCTION BY SOME TIME IN 1959. PREVIOUSLY 
THE WESTERN ALLIES HAD THOUCHT IN TERMS OF A TIMELAG OF ONLY A FEW 
MONTHS 

THE OTHER MODIFICAMION ENVISAGES A DECLARATION BY THE UNITED 
STATES, BRITAIN AND RUSSIA -- THE NUCLEAR THREE -- LIMITING THE USES OF 
ATOMIC AND HYDROGEN WEAPONS TO SELF-DEFENSE AGAINST MAJOR AGGRESSION. 
PREVIOUSLY THE WEST HAD REFUSED TO CONSIDER SPELLING OUT ANY FORM OF 
PROHIBITION ON THE USE OF THESE WEAPONS, 

HAROLD Es STASSEN, THE AMERICAN DISARMAMENT DELEGATE, WILL PRESENT 
THE NUCLEAR COMPONENT OF THE AMERICAN PLAN FOR A LIMITED DISARMAMENT 
TREATY TOMORROW WHEN THE FIVE-POWER SUBCOMMITTEE OF THE UNITED NATIONS 
DISARMAMENT COMMISSION RESUMES ITS TALKS IN LONDON. 

IN THE CONFERENCE OF BRITISH COMMONWEALTH STATESMEN TODAY, PRIME 
MINISTER JAWAHARLAL NEHRU OF INDIA, BACKED BY JUSTICE MINISTER M.W. 

DE SILVA OF CEYLON, PLEADED THAT BRITAIN TAKE THE LEAD IN CONCLUDING AN 
EAST-WEST ACCORD TO STOP NUCLEAR TESTS -- WITH OR WITHOUT CONDITIONS. 

CONFERENCE OFFICIALS SAID MOST OF THEIR COLLEAGUES DISAGREED. BRITI 

PRIME MINISTER HAROLD MACMILLAN, HIS FOREIGN SECRETARY 


AND OTHERS ARGUED THAT A BAN ON TESTS OF NUCLEAR ARMS AND ANY 


RENUNCIATION OF THEIR USE WOULD LEAVE RUSSIA AND RED CHINA IN A POSITION 


TO DOMINATE EUROPE AND ASIA. 

THE COMMONWEALTH LEADERS WERE SAID TO HAVE AGREED BROADLY THAT THE 
COMMUNIST CHINESE SHOULD BE BROUGHT INTO THE FINAL NEGOTIATIONS FOR ANY 
WORLD DISARMAMENT ARRANGEMENTS. THEY ARGUED THAT TO EXCLUDE RED CHINA 
WOULD RENDER ANY GLOBAL DISARMAMENT TREATY MEANINGLESS. 

INFORMANTS SAID THE COMMONWEALTH CHIEFS REALIZED THAT THE UNITED

BATH IS A QUIET, RESIDENTIAL CITY FAMOUS FOR ITS GEORGIAN 
ARCHITECTURE AS WELL AS ITS HEALING WATERS. BUT IT IS THE CENTER OF A

WITH ATOM BOMBS.

BATH AND CORSHAM. AT FILTON, 15 MILES AWAY, IS THE BRISTOL AEROPLANE

LASTS OUT THE SUMMER. BUT THERE IS LITTLE DOUBT THE BULK OF SOVIET

PEARL HARBOR. afLY 1 HEART AND BRAINS OF UeS. 
MILITARY ACTIVITY OVER Hi KE EARTH'S SURFACE WERE FORMALLY 4 (y)~ 
SENTERED TODAY AT THIS HISTORIC PACIFIC NAVAL BASE. 95 

FAR EASTERN AND PACIFIC COMMANDS WERE COMBINED UNDER A NAVY MAN. 

PEARL HARBOR,SCENE OF THE JAPANESE ATTACK THAT TOUCHED OFF 
THE PACIFIC PHASE OF WORLD WAR II DEC. 7, 1941, BECAME THE COMMAND 
POST FOR NEARLY A HALF MILLION UeS. SERVICEMEN AND MORE THAN 7,000 
PLANES AND 400 SHIPS ON GUARD BETWEEN AMERICAN AND COMMUNIST COASTS. 

BUT IT IS MORE THAN THAT. IN THE WORDS OF A HIGH OFFICER: 

FOR THE FIRST TIME IN OUR PACIFIC MILITARY HISTORY. THERE IS 
JUST ONE GUY TO SAY *DO IT*--ONE MILITARY BOSS WITH HIS SUBORDINATE 
COMMANDERS ON THE SAME ISLAND.® 

THE BOSS IS ADMsFELIX BsSTUMP, 62, A LANKY, PLAIN SPOKEN 
SAILOR-DIPLOMAT WHO LOOKS SOMETHING LIKE PRESIDENT EISENHOWER. THE 
CHANGE FOUND HIM IN TOKYO, WHERE THE FLAC OF GEN.DOUGLAS MACARTHUR'S 
OLD FAR EAST COMMAND WAS RAULED DOWN FOR THE LAST TIME. 

"WE HAVE THE FORCES NOW TO CONTAIN AN ATTACK THAT OCCURS ANYWHERE 
IN THE WORLD." THE ADMIRAL DECLARED. 

THE BULK OF U.S. COMBAT FORCES REMAIN RINGED ALONG THE 
PACIFIC DEFENSE PERIMETER FROM JAPAN TO THE PHILIPPINES. 

GEN. LAURENCE KUTER, THE AIR FORCE PACIFIC COMMANDER, SAID: 

*NONE OF OUR COMBAT FORCES IS MOVING FROM THE FAR EAST. IT'S 
A CASE OF THE QUARTERBACK MOVING INTO THE BACKFIELD." 

THERE IS STILL A FOUR-STAR QUARTERBACK FOR EACH SERVICE. 
STUMP WILL CALL THE SIGNALS AS TOP MAN 

HIS COMMAND COVERS 75 MILLION SQUARE MILES. THIS IS BORDERED BY 
8,000 MILES OF COMMUNIST COASTLINE--ABOUT FOUR TIMES THE LENGTH OF THE 
IRON CURTAIN IN EUROPE. IT INCLUDES SEVERAL OF THE WORLD'S MOST 
POTENTIALLY EXPLOSIVE AREAS, RED CHINA, KOREA AND VIET NAM, PLUS 
SUCH TOUCHY FRIENDLY AREAS AS JAPAN, FORMOSA AND THE PHILIPPINES. 

BESIDES UsSe FORCES, STUMP DIRECTS THE AMERICAN MILITARY ADVISORY 
GROUPS WHICH HANDLE TRAINING FOR SOME 1.700.000 TROOPS OF FRIENDLY 
PACIFIC NATIONS. HE IS ALSO TOP U.S. MILITARY ADVISER IN THE 
SEVEN~NATION SOUTHEAST ASIA TREATY ORGANIZATION (SEATO). |

___RED CHINA INTERPRETIVE 


[NGTC a MERICAN POLICY OF BOYCOTT OF RED 
aYCH F yeT BEEN IRMED BY SECRETARY OF STATE DULLES, 
TO BE HEADING INTO TROUBLE. 

VARIOUS PRESSURES ARE BUILDING UP AGAINST IT BOTH AT HOME AND ABROAD, 
AND THE EISENHOWER ADMINISTRATION MAY FIND IT IMPOSSIBLE TO HOLD THE 
LINE AT ALL POINTS IN THE NEXT TWO OR THREE YEARS. 

THE POLICY RESTATEMENT WAS MADE BY DULLES IN A SPEECH AT SAN 
FRANCISCO FRIDAY. IT WAS HIS FIRST MAJOR PRONOUNCEMENT ON THE UNITED 
STATES ATTITUDE TOWARD COMMUNIST CHINA IN THREE YEARS. OFFICIALS 
REPORTED THAT IT WAS FULLY APPROVED IN ADVANCE BY PRESIDENT EISENHOWER. 

AS AN OFFICIAL DECLARATION BY THE SECRETARY OF STATE UNDER THE : 
AUTHORIZATION OF THE PRESIDENT, THE SAN FRANCISCO SPEECH PRESUMABLY 
REPRESENTS THE CONSIDERED JUDGMENT OF THE ADMINISTRATION ON WHAT IS 
BEST FOR THE INTERESTS OF THE UNITED STATES IN DEALING WITH THE RED 
i) ® 

BUT THE SPEECH ALSO HAS THE EARMARKS OF A DOCUMENT IN A POLITICAL

AND REJECTED ALL ARGUMENTS WHICH HAVE BEEN ADVANCED FOR CHANGE. HE 
THEREFORE RECOGNIZED THAT HE HAS CRITICS TO DEAL WITH. 

HF DEALT EXPLICITLY WITH WHAT THE UNITED STATES SHOULD OR SHOULD 
NOT DO. HE LAID DOWN ANEW IN STRONG TERMS THE DECISION. THAT THIS 
“QUNTRY SHOULD NOT RECOGNIZE THE PEIPING REGIME, SHOULD NOT ENGAGE 
IN TRADE WITH IT, SHOULD NOT PERMIT CULTURAL CONTACTS AND SHOULD NOT 
ACREE TO ANY PLACE FOR RED CHINA IN THE UNITED NATIONS. 

HE SAID THAT AMERICAN POLICIES ARE *READILY ADJUSTABLE” TO MEET 
CHANGING CONDITIONS, BUT ADDED ®THERE ARE OCCASIONS WHEN OTHERS, AND 
NOT WE. SHOULD PROVIDE THE CHANGE.” 

IN EFFECT, HE SEEMED TO BE HOLDING OUT TO RED CHINA THE POSSIBILITY 
THAT IF IT WOULD CHANGE ITS WAYS THE UNITED STATES WOULD REVIEW ITS 
ATTITUDEe BALANCED AGAINST THIS WAS HIS ASSERTION THAT THE UNITED 
STATES EXPECTS THAT SOONER OR LATER THE CHINESE PEOPLE WILL RID THEM- 
SELVES OF COMMUNIST RULE AND THE REAL INTENTION OF THE UNITED STATES 
IS TO WAIT UNTIL THIS HAS COME ABOUT BEFORE OPENING UP FULL RELA- 
TIONS WITH THE MAINLAND OF CHINA | |

see bOeaneLON, JULY I CAP)-A FLEET OF 14 HELICOPTERS WILL CARRY 
THOWER AND STAFF TO A HIDEAWAY WHITE HOUSE AT SOME 

MOMENT DURING OPERATION ALERT 1957, THE FOURTH NATIONWIDE CIVIL 

DEFENSE EXERCISE STARTING JULY 12, IT WAS ANNOUNCED TODAY. 

ON THAT DAY ®ENEMY® BOMBERS WILL DUMP HYPOTHETICAL DESTRUCTION ON 
WASHINGTON AND SCORES OF OTHER CITIES, SETTING OFF A THREE-DAY 
PERIOD OF SIMULATED RESCUE, RELIEF AND EVACUATION, 

ON THE FOURTH DAY, JULY 15, SOME 7,500 GOVERNMENT WORKERS WILL 
REPORT TO 30-ODD RELOCATION CENTERS SECRETLY SET UP IN A HALF-DOZEN 
EASTERN STATES. THERE THEY WILL DIRECT THE RECONSTRUCTION AND WAR 

FORTS OF A PRESUMABLY DEVASTATED COUNTRY. 

WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY JAMES C.HAGERTY DISCLOSED THAT 
OPERATION ALERT HAS, IN FACT, ALREADY BEGUN IN A QUIET WAY. 

FOR TWO WEEKS, HE TOLD REPORTERS, DESIGNATED OFFICIALS HAVE BEEN 
OPERATING IN AN ASSUMED ATMOSPHERE OF “HEICHTENED INTERNATIONAL 
TENSION AND DETERIORATING INTERNATIONAL RELATIONS.” 

THEY HAVE DIRECTED THE MANNING AND EQUIPPING OF THE SECRET RE- 
LOCATION CENTERS. THAT IS "PHASE ONE" OF THE ALERT. } 

*PHASE TWO" --THE PERIOD OF ATTACK AND IMMEDIATE POST-ATTACK 
OPERATIONS--WILL INVOLVE PRIMARILY THE LOCAL AND STATE CIVIL DEFENSE 
ORGANIZATIONS AND THE FEDERAL CIVIL DEFENSE ADMINISTRATION (FCDA). 

THE CITIES TO BE BLASTED BY MOCK HYDROGEN AND ATOMIC BOMBS WILI BE 
ADVISED OF THEIR FATE JUST BEFORE THE EXERCISE. IN THFORY THE 
IDENTITY OF THE TARGETS, THE EXTENT OF DAMAGE AND THE PATHS OF 
RADIOACTIVE FALLOUT WILL NOT BE KNOWN TO FCDA UNTIL REPORTS HAVE 
BEEN RELAYED FROM LOCAL TO STATE FCDA OFFICES AND THUS TO FCDA 

"PHASE THREE,® JULY 15-19, WILL BE THE PERIOD OF FEDERAL COVERNMENT 
OPERATION IN THE FIELD. IT WILL ASSUME THAT 15 DAYS HAVE PASSED SINCE 
THE BOMBS FEL], AND DAMAGE HAS BEEN APPRAISED AND WAR IS RACING. 

THE FEDERAL OFFICIALS WILL RE HANDED THE PROBLEMS OF RESTORING 


MILITARY AND CIVILIAN ate etirel RE-ESTABLISHING TRANSPORTATION 


AND COMMUNICATIONS, ADMIN STERING WAGES, PRICE, PRIORITY AND OTHER 
CONTROLS AND SUPPORTING AN ALL-OUT MILITARY EFFORT.

THE EMERGENCY WHITE HOUSE HAVE NOT YET BEEN FIXED.

HIDEAWAY AND ITS OPERATION, HAGERTY SAID, AND THEN WILL RETURN TO

IN FULL SWING IN MID-JULY. 

BUT THE WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY JAMES C. HAGERTY TOLD NEWSMEN 
YESTERDAY THAT FOR TWO WEEKS, CERTAIN KEY OFFICIALS HAVE BEEN AT WORK 
MANNING AND EQUIPPING SECRET RELOCATION CENTERS. FROM THESE CENTERS, 
PICKED GOVERNMENT TEAMS WILL DIRECT SIMULATED RECONSTRUCTION AND A 
MOCK WAR EFFORT IN THE WAKE OF AN ASSUMED NUCLEAR ATTACK ON THE UN- 


ITED STATES. 
AT ONE STAGE OF EXER HAGERTY SAID, PRESIDENT EISENHOWER

AND HIS STAFF WILL BE FLOWN TO A SECRET COMMAND

EMERGENCY WHITE HOUSE BEFORE RETURNING TO WASHINGTON. THE DAY AND HOUR 
OF HIS TRIP HAVE NOT YET BEEN DETERMINED.

THAT DAY. WASHINGTON AND SCORES OF OTHER CITIES WILL BE "DESTROYED. 
THIS WILL BEGIN "PHASE TWO" OF THE OPERATION--A THREE-DAY PERIOD OF 
PRETENDED RESCUE. RELIEF AND EVACUATION. THIS PHASE WILL INVOLVE 
CHIEFLY CIVIL DEFENSE ORGANIZATIONS ON THE LOCAL, STATE AND FEDERAL 

oS

SUPPORTING AN ALL-OUT MILITARY EFFORT.

MOSCOW, THURSDAY, JULY &amp; CAP)-THE KREMLIN HAS EXPELLED GEORG Ec 
MALENKOV, Ve Me MOLOTOV, LeM. KAGANOVICH AND DMITRI SHEPILOV FROM 
THEIR HIGH POSTS IN THE SOVIET COMMUNIST PARTY. THEY WERE ACCUSED 
OF COLLUSION AND INTRIGUE AGAINST THE PARTY'S LEADERSHIP. 

APPARENTLY THE CENTRAL COMMITTEE STOPPED SHORT OF THE SEVERE 
PENALTY OF EXPELLING THEM FROM THE COMMUNIST PARTY, AS SOME COMMITTEE 
MEMBERS HAD URGED. INSTEAD, IT EXPELLED THEM FROM’ THE CENTRAL 
COMMITTEE AND THE PRESIDIUM’ (POLITBURO). 

THE CENTRAL COMMITTEE ELECTED A NEW PRESIDIUM INCLUDING MARSHAL 
GEORGI Ke puuxay WORLD WAR II HERO OF MOSCOW, AND MRS. 

EKATERINA URTSEVA THE FIRST WOMAN ON THE RULING PARTY BODY.

FAR-REACHING SHAKEUP TO A MASS MEETING OF COMMUNIST PARTY MEMBERS 
APPARENTLY CONVENED IN THE KREMLIN, EXPLAINING THAT THE FOUR ACCUSED 
HAD BEEN DECISIVELY CONDEMNED FOR ANTI-PARTY ACTIVITIES "DIRECTED AT 
BREAKING UP THE PARTY.®

AND MeGe PE N, TWO LEADING ECONOMIC AND INDUSTRIAL EXPERTS OF 
THE SOVIET UNTON, ALSO HAD BEEN DEMOTED. THEY WERE NOT LISTED AS 
MEMBERS OR ALTERNATES OF THE NEW PRESIDIUM, ALTHOUGH THE OFFICIAL

®2, TO EXCLUDE COMRADES MALENKOV, KAGANOVICH AND MOLOTOV FROM THE

YESTERDAY PRAVDA, SIGNALING EVENTS TO COME, HAD CARRIED A FULL 
PAGE ARTICLE ON THE SUBJECT OF DISSENSIONS IN PARTY RANKS AND THE NEED 
FOR *UNSHAKABLE UNITY.° 


THE POLICY vt PRANCLPLE IS THE ONLY RIGHT POLICY,” PRAVDA SAID. 
"THE BEDROCK PRINCIPLE OF COMMUNISTS IS NEVER TO DEPART IN ANYTHING 
FROM THE COMMON GENERAL PARTY INTERESTS. 

*IT WAS THIS ONLY RIGHT PRINCIPLE THAT THE PARTY AND ITS FOUNDER, 
LENIN, ALWAYS TOOK AS THEIR GUIDE IN TREATMENT OF ANYONE WHO DIS- 
REGARDED THE WILL OF THE PARTY AND ITS INTERESTS OR OPPOSED ITS LINE, 
NO MATTER HOW GREAT THE SERVICES AND PRESTIGE OF THESE PEOPLE, NOR 
HOW HIGH THEIR POSITION.® 

PPRAVDA RECALLED THAT LENIN DID NOT HESITATE TO CONDEMN ONE OF 
HIS CLOSEST ASSOCIATES, GEORGI Ve PLEKHANOV, ONE OF THE PRE-REVOLUTION

LONDON, THURSDAY, JULY 4&amp; (AP)-THE FIRING OF FOUR LEADERS OF THE SO- 
VIET COMMUNIST PARTY WAS VIEWED HERE TODAY AS A SWEEPING AWAY OF THE | 
REMAINING STALINISTS IN THE PARTY HIERARCHY. 

EXPERTS IN SOVIET AFFAIRS CALLED IT A VICTORY FOR NIKITA S. 
KHRUSHCHEV. 

IN BELGRADE, YUGOSLAVIA, OBSERVERS SAID KHRUSHCHEV AND HIS GROUP» 
QUIETLY STRUGGLING FOR PREBCOMINANCEs FINALLY HAD SUCCEEDED IN MUSTER- 
ING ENOUGH SUPPORT FOR A SHOWDOWN WITH THE STALINISTS. 

THE PURGE WILL HAVE BIG POLITICAL REPERCUSSIONS IN YUGOSLAVIA. THE 
FOUR TOP MEN PURGED FROM THE LEADERSHIP WERE ACCUSED OF STANDING IN THE 
WAY OF A RESUMPTION OF NORMAL RELATIONS WITH BELGRADE AND OF RESISTING 
BASE OF THE BELGRADE-MOSCOW SPLIT TOUCHED OFF BY STALIN IN 1948. ~ . |

®THIS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO SOVIET FOREIGN POLICY’S GAINING BROADER 
CONFIDENCE AND PRESTIGE IN THE WORLD. IN VIEW OF THE FACT THAT PERSONS 
WHO IMPEDED THE STRONGER AFFIRMATION OF A POLICY OF PEACE AND ACTIVE 
COEXISTENCE HAVE BEEN REMOVED FROM SOVIET ACTIVE POLICY, THIS ACTUALLY 
CONSTITUTES A FURTHER MAJOR VICTORY OF THE CAUSE OF PEACE AND COOPERA- 
TION AMONG NATIONS."

A SMALL CREW OF STATE DEPARTMENT EXPERTS WORKED THROUGH THE JULY 
4&amp; HOLIDAY TO KEEP TRACK OF MOSCOW DEVELOPMENTS, SUCH AS THE OUSTER

KAGANOVITCH. THEY AND DMITRI SHEPILOV HAD ALREADY LOST THEIR KEY 


THE TRIP OBVIOUSLY WAS INTENDED TO SHOWPOSITIONS IN THE HIGH COMMAND OF THE COMMUNIST PARTY. 


THERE WAS NO SENSE OF CRISIS OR EXCITEMENT APPARENT HERE, AS 
WOULD HAVE BEEN THE CASE IF THERE HAD BEEN A REAL CHANGE IN TOP 
GOVERNMENT CONTROL. PRESIDENT EISENHOWER WAS RELAXING AT GETTYSBURG 
AND SECRETARY OF STATE DULLES AT HIS ISLAND RETREAT IN LAKE ONTARIO. 
BUT NOBODY MINIMIZED THE IMPORTANCE OF THE MOSCOW CHANGES. 
KHRUSHCHEV NOW IS STRONGER THAN EVER AND POSSIBLY HAS THE OPPORTUNITY 
OF MAKING HIMSELF A DICTATOR, WHETHER THAT WILL HAPPEN NO ONE 
CAN PREDICT. IT WOULD DEPEND ON HIS OWN MOTIVATIONS, AND THE 
RESTRAINTS WHICH MIGHT BE EXERCISED ON HIM BY SUCH MEN AS MARSHALL 
GEORGI ZHUKOV. THE DEFENSE MINISTER AND ARMY SPOKESMAN WHO HAS NOW 
BECOME A MEMBER OF THE PRESIDIUM. 


KHRUSHCHEV HAS BEEN INVOLVED IN POLICY DISPUTES EVER SINCE HE 
TOOK OVER PARTY CONTROL AFTER THE DEATH OF STALIN IN MARCH 1955. 
IN ONE OF THESE=--OVER THE RELATIVE PRIORITIES TO BE ASSIGNED PRO- 
DUCTION OF CONSUMER GOODS AND HEAVY MACHINERY--HE FIRED MALENKOV 
AS PREMIER AND NIKOLAI BULGANIN MOVED UP. MALENKOV HAD SPOKEN OUT 
FOR MORE CONSUMER GOODS IN WHAT WAS REGARDED ABROAD AS A BID FOR 
POPULARITY IN RUSSIA. 

KHRUSHCHEV HAS APPEARED TO MANY EXPERTS HERE TO BE A HARD-BOILED, 
EMINENTLY PRACTICAL MAN WITH THE SAME DEDICATION TO THE WORLD-WIDE 
TRIUMPH OF COMMUNISM AS STALIN PROFESSED BUT WITH FAR GREATER RESOURCE- 
FULNESS AND AGILITY IN DRIVING TOWARD THAT GOAL. 

KHRUSHCHEV HAS LIFTED THE STALINIST YOKE FROM THE EASTERN 
EUROPEAN SATELLITE COUNTRIES~--ALTHOUGH HE REIMPOSED IT RUTHLESSLY 
ON HUNGARY IN THE BLOOD BATH WHICH FOLLOWED THE ANTI-COMMUNIST REVOLT 
LAST OCTOBER. HE HAS SEEMED TO GRANT A LITTLE MORE FREEDOM INSIDE 
RUSSIA, ALTHOUGH FOREIGN DIPLOMATS FIND THAT GREAT AREAS OF THE 
COUNTRY ARE STILL UNDER _AN IRON CURTAIN OF MENACING SECRECY. 

WITH RESPECT TO FOREIGN POLICY, KHRUSHCHEV HAS TALKED DOWN THE 
CHANCES OF ARMED CONFLICT AND TALKED UP THE CONTEST OF POLITICAL 
AND ECONOMIC FORCES BETWEEN THE COMMUNIST AND FREE WORLDS. HOWEVER. 





HE OCCASIONALLY RELAPSES INTO A KIND OF CLASSIC KREMLIN ATTACK ON THE 
UNITED STATES AS A THREAT TO WORLD PEACE.

BY ERNEST Be VACCARO 

(ADVANCE) WASHINGTON, JULY 4 (AP)-SEN. HUMPHREY (D-MINN) PROPOSED 
TONIGHT THE CREATION OF AN INTERNATIONAL AGENCY TO DEVELOP THE RE- 
SOURCES OF THE MIDDLE EAST AND HELP RESOLVE THE ARABIAN-ISRAFLI 

HE SAID EFFORTS TO SET UP A MIDDLE EAST DEVELOPMENT AGENCY SHOULD 
BE ACCOMPANIED BY AMERICAN INSISTENCE THAT ISRAEL AND THE ARAB 
STATES SEEK A SETTLEMENT OF THEIR DIFFERENCES THROUGH "DIRECT 
NEGOTIATIONS,” 

"AFTER 10 YEARS OF TEMPORIZING WITH THIS SITUATION,” HE SAID, “IT 
IS TIME FOR THE NATIONS INVOLVED TO COME TO TERMS--AND THE ONLY WAY 
OF PRODUCING A SETTLEMENT ACCEPTABLE TO BTOTH SIDES. AND THEREFORE 
DURABLE, IS BY INSISTING THAT THEY REACH A SETTLEMENT THEMSELVES." 

HUMPHREY MADE HIS RECOMMENDATIONS IN A DETAILED REPORT TO THE 
SENATE FOREIGN RELATIONS COMMITTEE ON HIS RECENT VISIT TO THE AREA. 

UNDER HIS PLAN, THE DEVELOPMENT AGENCY WOULD BE SET UP WITHIN THE 
FRAMEWORK OF THE UNITED NATIONS. 

IT WOULD UNDERTAKE PROJECTS ITSELF, LEND MONEY TO EITHER PRIVATE OR 
PUBLIC “AGENCIES, MANAGE PROJECTS; CARRY ON RESEARCH IN SOIL FERTILITY 
AND MAKE BASIC ENGINEERING SURVEYS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF ALL THE 
STATES IN THE MIDDLE EAST. 

"IT COULD," HUMPHREY SAID, "WORK OUT A SOLUTION TO THE WHOLE PAL- 
ESTINE-ARAB REFUGEE PROBLEM" AND ENCOURAGE INTERNATIONAL ACCEPTANCE OF 
PLANS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE JORDAN AND OTHER RIVERS FOR THE 

THE ONLY POSSIBLE SOLUTION OF THE PROBLEM OF THE 900,000 "ROOTLESS, 
JOBLESS, DISILLUSIONED, AND EMBITTERED® REFUGEES, HE SAID, IS TO 
PROVIDE *PERMANENT HOMES AND TOLERABLE LIVELIHOODS IN THE ARAB 
STATES "FOR A MAJORITY OF THEM. HE ALSO PROPOSED THAT ISRAEL PLEDGE 
"TO ACCEPT A LIMITED NUMBER OF TOKEN REPATRIATES." 

HE SAID THAT HALF OF THE REFUGEES ARE UNDER 15 YEARS OLD, THAT THEY 
AAVE NO ROOTS IN PALESTINE AT ALL, AND THEIR DESTINY LIES’ IN "AN 
OPPORTUNITY FOR A PRODUCTIVE AND SELF-RELIANT LIFE IN AN ARAB

WASHINGTON, JULY 5 CAP)-U.S. FOREIGN ASSISTANCE OF ALL KINDS TOTALED 
ALMOST 1 1/4 BILLION DOLLARS IN THE FIRST THREE MONTHS OF 1957. THIS 
WAS ABOUT 30 PER CENT MORE THAN IN THE LAST THREE MONTHS OF 1956. 

JAMES We. MCNALLY, ACTING DIRECTOR OF THE COMMERCE DEPARTMENT'S 
OFFICE OF BUSINESS ECONOMICS, DISCLOSED THE FICURES TODAY IN A REPORT 
DISTRIBUTED AS "PREPARED FOR USE OF CONGRESS AND COVERNMENT ACEN- 

THE FIGURE OF ALMOST 1 1/4 BILLION, AS USED BY THE DEPARTMENT 
INCLUDED 993 MILLION DOLLARS IN NET TRANSFERS UNDER GRANT AND CREDIT 
PROGRAMS PLUS 246 MILLION DOLLARS IN SHORT-TERM CLAIMS ON FORFICN 
COUNTRIES THROUGH ACCEPTANCE OF THEIR CURRENCIES IN PAYMENT FOR FARM 
PRODUCTS EXPORTED FROM THE UNITED STATES. 

MILITARY GRANT DELIVERIES IN 1957 INCREASED BY ABOUT ONE-HALF. TO 
620 MILLION DOLLARS. OTHER GRANTS DECLINED BY ONE-FIFTH TO 380 MILLION 
DOLLARS (NET). LOAN DISBURSEMENTS WERE ABOUT UNCHANGED AT 118 MILLION 
DOLLARS AND WERE ALMOST EQUAL TO PRINCIPAL REPAYMENTS OF 122 MILLION 

*€ 

MCNALLY SAID THE RECENT TREND IN GEOGRAPHICAL DISTRIBUTION CON- 
TINUED, WITH WESTERN EUROPE RECEIVING THE CREATER PART OF THE 
MILITARY DELIVERIES, AND THE ASIAN AREAS MORE THAN HALF OF OTHER CRANTS 
AND CREDITS AND SHORT-TERM ASSISTANCE. 

THE UNITED STATES HAS MADE NEARLY 59 BILLION DOLLARS IN POST WAR 
NET FOREIGN GRANT AND CREDIT TRANSFERS. IN ADDITION. IT HAS INVESTED 
$3,400,000,000 (B) IN THREE INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS AND 
ABCuT ONE AND ONE-THIRD BILLION DOLLARS THROUGH THE EXCHANCE OF 
AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS FOR FOREIGN CURRENCIES WHICH IT HAS NOT DIs-

NATIONWIDE HOOKUP DIRECT FROM THE SCENE

(ADVANCE) WASHINGTON, JULY 6 (AP)-SEVEN REPUBLICAN AND THREE 
DEMOCRATIC SENATONS-URCEDSENTOEASTOAND (D-NiGSs TODAY TO SCHEDULE 
"IMMEDIATE HEARINGS" ON LEGISLATION TO LIBERALIZE IMMIGRATION LAWS AND 
EASE THE PLIGHT OF HUNGARIAN REFUGEES. 

EASTLAND IS CHAIRMAN OF THE SENATE JUDICIARY COMMITTEE AND ITS IMMIGRA 
TION SUBCOMMITTEE. SO FAR THIS SESSION HE HAS NOT HELD HEARINGS ON 
ANY IMMIGRATION LEGISLATION, INCLUDING THE PROGRAM SUBMITTED BY PRESI- 
DENT EISENHOWER. 

IN A LETTER TO HIM, THE 10 SENATORS SAID "THE TIME HAS COME FOR YOUR 
COMMITTEE TO TAKE AFFIRMATIVE ACTION IF ANY PROGRESS IS TO BE MADE ON 
THIS VITAL PROBLEM AT THIS SESSION OF THE CONGRESS, AS WE ARE DEEPLY 
CONVINCED IT MUST BE IN THE NATIONAL INTEREST." 

THE LETTER WAS MADE PUBLIC BY SEN. JAVITS (R-NY). HE LISTED THOSE 
WHO HAD JOINED HIM IN SIGNING IT AS SENS. BEALL (MD), BUSH (CONN), 

CASE (NJ), COOPER (KY), IVES (NY) AND PAYNE (ME). ALL. REPUBLICANS 
AND_SENS. DOUGLAS (ILL$, HUMPHREY (MINN) AND NEUBERGER (ORE): DEMOCRATS. 
THE PROGRAM SUBMITTED BY EISENHOWER LAST JAN. 31 CALLS FOR REVISION 
OF THE BASIC MCCARRAN-WALTER IMMIGRATION ACT TO PERMIT INCREASED IMMICRA 
TION TO THIS COUNTRY, PARTICULARLY FROM COUNTRIES IN SOUTHERN AND 

SOUTHEASTERN EUROPE. 

HE ALSO ASKED CONGRESS TO GRANT PERMANENT RESIDENCE TO HUNGARIAN 
REFUGEES ADMITTED TO THIS COUNTRY ON A TEMPORARY EMERGENCY BASIS AFTER 
LAST FALL'S FREEDOM REVOLT IN THEIR COMMUNIST-RULED HOMELAND. 





T NT'S PROPOSALS WOULD AUTHORIZE THE ADMISSION 
EACH YEAR OF A&amp; MANY Ae 66-000 FUTURE ESCAPEES FROM COMMUNIST TYRANNY.

PENDING IMMIGRATION MEASURES, SAID THE ANTI-COMMUNIST UP ISING IN

CAP)-RUSSIA MAY BE WELL STARTED ON THE WAY T

THE SUSPICION IS GROWING IN OFFICIAL QUARTERS HERE THAT THIS IS THE 
REAL MEANING BEHIND RUSSIA’S RECENTLY DISCLOSED SALE TO EGYPT OF THREE 

ONE OF EGYPT*S PURPOSES IN OBTAINING THE UNDERSEA CRAFT MAY LIE IN 
USING THEM TO TRY TO PREVENT THE PASSAGE OF SHIPS THROUGH THE GULF 
OF AQABA TO THE ISRAELI PORT OF EILAT. EGYPT AND OTHER ARAB STATES 
CONTEND THAT THE GULF Is ARAB TERRITORIAL WATER AND THAT SHIPPING 
TO ISRAEL CA “ 

TWO OF THE SUBMARINES, WHICH ARRIVED SOME TIME AGO AT THE PORT OF 
ALEXANDRIA, ARE DESCRIBED BY AUTHORITIES HERE AS CAPABLE OF LAYING 
MINES. THE ULTIMATE EGYPTIAN INTENTION MAY BE TO TRY TO MINE THE 
WATERS AT THE ENTRANCE TO THE GULF, WHICH OPENS OFF THE RED SEA. 

BUT WHAT INTRIGUES AND WORRIES AMERICAN EXPERTS EVEN MORE IS WHAT 
MAY BE BEHIND RUSSIA'S SALE OF THE UUNDERWATER CRAFT. 

IN THE VIEW OF RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITIES WHO HAVE ANALYZED THE DEAL, 
POSSESSION AND OPERATION OF THE SUBMARINES BY EGYPT WILL MEAN THAT 
ECYPT WILL HAVE TO BUILD UP A SUBMARINE OPERATING BASE POSSIBLY AT 
ALEXANDRIA. 

WITH PRESIDENT NASSER*S EGYPTIAN GOVERNMENT ALREADY CLOSELY LINKED 
WITH THE SOVIET UNION, SUUCH A BASE WOULD BE RUSSIAN EQUIPPED. IT 
COULD EASILY BE SUPPLIED WITH A LARGE STORE OF REPAIR PARTS AND WITH 
OTHER MATERIALS AND THE FUEL SUITABLE FOR SUBMARINE OPERATIONS. 

ONCE SUCH A BASE IS ESTABLISHED IT COULD READILY BE USED BY THE 
SOVIETS* OWN SUBMARINES AS WELL AS THOSE UNDER THE EGYPTIAN FLAG. 
RUSSIAN TECHNICIANS COULD BE AVAILABLE THERE TO SERVICE VISITING SOVIE 
UNDERWATER VESSELS. 

IN SUCH A CASE WASHINGTON OFFICIALS WOULD EXPECT THAT SUCH VISITS 
WOULD BE CARRIED OUT WITH CONSIDERABLE FREQUENCY. 

THE PRESENCE OF THE SOVIET SUBMARINES IN MEDITERRANEAN WATERS 
WOULD THEN BECOME A FACTOR WHICH STRATEGIC PLANNERS OF THE WESTERN 
POWERS WOULD HAVE TO TAKE CONSTANTLY INTO CONSIDERATION. 

THE POSSIBILITY OF RUSSIA*S SCORING SUCH A STRATEGIC GAIN IS CON-

BY EDWIN Be HAAKINSON 
_ (ADVANCE WASHINGTON, JULY 7. CAP)-SENe-HUMPHREY (D-MINN) TODAY URGED 
A “FRESH LOOK AT OUR POLICY® TOWARD RED CHINA AND A REVISION OF THE 
1953 TRUCE THAT ENDED THE KOREAN FICHTING. 
HIS PROPOSALS, WHICH APPEARED TO RUN COUNTER TO THOSE OF SECRETARY 
OF STATE DULLES AND OTHER ADMINISTRATION LEADERS, APPEARED IN A FORE- 
WORD TO A COMMITTEE STAFF STUDY OF DISARMAMENT PROBLEMS IN ASIAc 
IT IS ESSENTIAL THAT COMMUNIST CHINA BE BROUGHT INTO ANY DIS- 
ARMAMENT SYSTEM AT AN EARLY STAGE," HUMPHREY, CHAIRMAN OF A SPECIAL 
SENATE DISARMAMENT COMMITTEE. SAID. 
UNLESS THIS IS DONE, THE SENATOR SAID. THE PEIPING COMMUNIST coV- 
ERNMENT *WILL PROVIDE A LOOPHOLE WHICH THE SOVIET UNION MICHT USE 
TO VIOLATE OBLIGATIONS UNDERTAKEN AS A RESULT OF A DISARMAMENT AGREE- 


MENT 

HUMPHREY PROPOSED THAT THIS COUNTRY ACCEPT RED CHINA'S OFFER TO 
ADMIT Us. Se NEWSMEN BEHIND ®THE BAMBOO CURTAIN.® 

®WE SHOULD CONSIDER MODIFYING OTHER BARRIERS. SUCH AS 
THE TRADE EMBARGO, WHICH FORCE CHINA INTO EVER CLOSER RELATIONS WITH 
THE SOVIET BLOC.® HE ADDED. 

# = "AS LONG AS THERE ARE NO ARMAMENT CONTROLS ON COMMUNIST CHINA, 
THAT COUNTRY WILL BE FREE TO CONTINUE TO STRENCTHEN ITS LARCE MILI- 
TARY MACHINE," HE SAID. 

IN KOREA, HUMPHREY SAID CONTINUED VIOLATIONS BY THE NORTH KOREAN 
COMMUNISTS OF THE 1953 AGREEMENT NOT TO REARM, REQUIRE A REVISION 
OF THE PRESENT ARMISTICE AGREEMENT. 

THE SENATOR PROPOSED THAT THE UNITED NATIONS TAKE LEADERSHIP IN 
THIS MOVE AND PROVIDE FOR "A THINNING OUT OF ARMED FORCES AND ARMAMENTS 
ON BOTH SIDES OF THE ARMISTICE LINES AND FOR EFFECTIVE MUTUAL INSPEC - 
TION, 

HUMPHREY SAID THIS COULD INCLUDE *MUTUAL AERIAL AND GROUND INSPEC- 
TION OF THE TYPE THAT BOTH THE UNITED STATES AND SOVIET RUSSIA HAVE 
ALREADY A ‘ 

®SUCH AN AGREEMENT WOULD AMELIORATE A DANGEROUS SITUATION IN KOREA 
AND PERHAPS PAVE THE WAY FOR A POLITICAL SETTLEMENT,” HE SAID. | 

HUMPHREY SAID THE PROBLEMS OF RED CHINA ®AFTER BEING STALLED ON 
DEAD CENTER FOR HALF A DOZEN YEARS, ARE NOW APPROACHING A DECISIVE 
JUNCTURE. 

RELATIONS WITH THIS COUNTRY HAVE BEEN DEADLOCKED, HE SAID, OVER 
FAILURE OF RED CHINA TO RELEASE AMERICAN PRISONERS DESPITE LONG NEGO- 
TIATIONS. 

HUMPHREY SAID SIX AMERICANS STILL ARE BEING HELD PRISONER AND COM- 
MUNIST LEADERS *SHOULD REALIZE THAT RELEASE OF THOSE IMPRISONED WOULD 
HELP TO LESSEN : 

THEIR RELEASE. HE SAID, °SHOULD OPEN THE GATE TO NEGOTIATIONS ON 
OTHER DIFFERENCES, THE RESOLUTION OF WHICH WOULD HELP DISSIPATE 
ILL-AFFORDED ARMS BURDENS NOW WEIGHING UPON RED CHINA, THE NATIONS TO 
THE SOUTH AND SOUTHEASTERN ASIA, AS WELL AS OTHER COUNTRIES.

AT THE MOMENT, THEY BELIEVE HE IS FULLY SUPPORTING THE TOP MAN,

THEY SEEM INCLINED NOW TO CREDIT ZHUKOV WITH A POSSIBLY DECISIVE 
ROLE IN CRUSHING THE CHALLENGE TO KHRUSHCHEV’S NO. 1 POSITION DURING 
THE STORMY KREMLIN DEVELOPMENTS OF THE PAST TWO WEEKS. 

ZHUKOV, AS A REPRESENTATIVE OF THE RED ARMY, THEY BELIEVE, CAN BE 
EXPECTED TO PLAY AN INCREASINGLY IMPORTANT ROLE, ESPECIALLY NOW THAT 
HE HAS BEEN ELEVATED TO FULL MEMBERSHIP IN THE PARTY PRESIDIUM. 

THIS AMOUNTS TO AN AMAZING COMEBACK FOR THE SOVIET WAR HERO WHO 
UNTIL A LITTLE MORE THAN FOUR YEARS AGO WAS IN EFFECT EXILED BY 
STALIN TO A RELATIVELY OBSCURE ARMY COMMAND IN THE CRIMEA. 

ZHUKOV’S BACKING OF KHRUSHCHEV HAS SET SOME OFFICIALS TO WONDERING 
WHAT THIS SUPPORT HAS COST THE SOVIET PARTY CHIEF. THE QUESTION THEY 
ASK IS: HAS KHRUSHCHEV BEEN FORCED TO BECOME A CAPTIVE OF THE RED 
ARMY IN ORDER TO SURVIVE THE STRUGGLE FOR POWER? 

THE INCREASINGLY IMPORTANT ROLE OF THE ARMY DURING THE PAST YEAR 
IN SOVIET GOVERNMENT AFFAIRS IS DETECTED IN SUCH EXAMPLES AS BIRTHDAY 
GREETINGS EXTENDED TO IMPORTANT GENERAL OFFICERS ON THEIR 50TH 

THE SUDDEN SHAKE-UP WHICH RESULTED IN THE OUSTER OF SIX TOP 
KREMLIN LEADERS, OFFICIALS BELIEVE, UNDOUBTEDLY HAS ADDED TO THE ARMY 
INFLUENCE WITHIN THE INNER CIRCLE. 

MOST AUTHORITIES, WHILE VIEWING KHRUSHCHEV AS UNCHALLENGED SOVIET 
LEADER, NEVERTHELESS BELIEVE HE WILL KEEP THE "COLLECTIVE LEADERSHIP" 
WHICH HAS BEEN BUILT UP SINCE STALIN’S DEATH. BUT, AN INCREASINGLY 
IMPORTANT NUMBER OF OFFICIALS SEEM TO BE VEERING TQ THE IDEA THAT 


KHRUSHCHEV HAS NOW EMBARKED ON A DRIVE TO BECOME A STALIN-LIKE DICTATOR 


WHOSE EVERY WORD IS TO BE FOLLOWED.

UP THE HUGE ABADAN OIL REFINERIES. 

GEN. TEIMOUR BAKHTIAR, WHO IS ALSO DEPUTY PREMIER TOLD A NEWS 
CONFERENCE IRAN HAD ARRESTED A NUMBER OF COMMUNISTS *WHO WERE ALMOST 
READY*® TO PUT INTO OPERATION THE PLAN TO SABOTAGE THE REFINERIES» 

THE REFINERIES AT ABADAN ARE OPERATED UNDER A JOINT AGREEMENT 
BETWEEN IRAN AND A GROUP OF EIGHT OIL COMPANIES OWNED BY BRITISH, 
AMERICAN, DUTCH AND FRENCH INTERESTS. THEY ARE THE FORMER 
PROPERTIES OF THE NATIONALIZED ANGLO-IRANIAN OIL CO. 


THE COMMUNISTS HAD ASSEMBLED BLAST EQUIPMENT, BAKHTIAR SAID, BUT 
WERE CAPTURED RED-HANDED A FEW HOURS BEFORE THE’ ZERO HOUR. 

THE GENERAL SAID THE PLOTTERS WERE GOING TO USE A DYNAMITE HAND 
GRENADE, ALTHOUGH A FLAMING MATCH, APPLIED IN SOME PLACES, WOULD BE 
ENOUGH tO BLOW UP THE WHOLE OF ABADAN. 

THE NAMES OF THE CAPTIVES WERE NOT DISCLOSED, BUT BAKHTIAR 
SPECIFIED THAT THEY WERE CLOSELY ATTACHED TO MOSCOW AGENTS IN IRAN. 

IRAN'S COMMUNIST PARTY (TUDEH) HAS BEEN OPERATING SECRETLY DESPITE 
THE FACT IT IS OUTLAWED AND THAT ITS LEADERS ARE LIABLE TO BE SHOT 
OR JAILED. THIRTY COMMUNIST LEADERS, MOSTLY ARMY OFFICERS, WERE 
EXECUTED IN 1954 AFTER A SECRET TRIAL.

TO SUPPLY THE NEEDED NUMBER OF PROTONS AND ELECTRONS. 

WHEN JOHN MILSTED OF BRITAIN’S HARWELL ESTABLISHMENT WORKED AT 
ARGONNE LAST SUMMER UNDER THE U.S. BRITISH EXCHANGE PROGRAM, FIELDS AND 
FRIEDMAN DISCUSSED THE EXPERIMENT WITH HIM.

LENNART HOLM.

MEANING OF AGGRESSION MAY BE THE KEY TO AGREEMENT ON USE OF NUCLEAR

SUGGESTIONS BY ZORIN THAT THE UNITED STATE 
TRYING TO REACH AGREEMENT ON BOTH NUCLEAR MATTERS AND A GENERAL

USING ITS NUCLEAR KNOW-HOW MAINLY TO PRODUCE NEW WEAPONS OF MASS

MALENKOV WAS MADE PREMIER AFTER THE DEATH OF STALIN IN 1953. 

TWO YEARS LATER HE WAS DEPOSED BY PARTY BOSS NIKITA S.KHRUSHCHEV AND 
GIVEN THE DIRECTION OF ALL THE NATION'S ELECTRIC POWER STATIONS WITH 
THE RANK OF MINISTER. 

NOW HE GOES TO A JOB IN A TOWN FOUR MILES FROM THE CLOSEST RAIL 
STATION. 

SINCE THE NEWS OF MALENKOV’S PURGING WAS ANNOUNCED LAST WEEK 
MALENKOV HAS BEEN ACCUSED OF MASTER-MINDING THE PLOT THAT PURGED

SABOTAGE SOVIET GOVERNMENT POLICY, AND TRYING TO ORGANIZE ILLEGAL 
OPPOSITION TO THE COMMUNIST PARTY LEADERSHIP.

WASHINGTON, JULY 10 (AP)-THE AGRICULTURE DEPARTMENT PREDICTED TODAY 
THAP-POON DEFLCITS 
FROM RE-EMERGING THIS YEAR AS A MAJOR COMPETITOR OF UeS. FARMERS IN 
WESTERN EUROPE. 

AT TIMES IN THE PAST, EAST EUROPE HAS BEEN A BIG SUPPLIER FOR 
THE WESTERN PART OF THE’ CONTINENT. BUT IT HAS HAD MUCH LESS Foon To 
EXPORT IN POSTWAR YEARS THAN IN PRE-WAR TIMES. 

IN A REPORT ON EUROPE'S EAST-WEST FOOD TRADE, THE DEPARTMENT'S 
FOREIGN AGRICULTURAL SERVICE SAID "IT IS CLEAR THAT NOT ONLY EAST 
EUROPE AS A WHOLE BUT ALSO THE SOVIET BLOC ALONE BECAME A NET IMPORTER 
IN 1955 AND 1956." 

"IMPORTS WILL PROBABLY CONTINUE TO EXCEED EXPORTS IN 1957 AT LEAST," 
THE REPORT SAID. "THE 1956 GRAIN AND OILSEED CROPS IN THE DANUBE 
BASIN AND THE SUGAR BEET CROPS IN EAST GERMANY, CZECHOSLOVAKIA AND 
POLAND WERE POOR. 

"MOREOVER, WHILE THE SOVIET UNION HAD A LARGE GRAIN CROP, IT ALSO 
INCREASED IT&amp; 1957 EXPORT COMMITMENTS TO OTHER EAST EUROPEAN COUNTRIES, 
PARTLY TO HELP OFFSET THE POOR HARVEST IN THE SOUTHEAST AND PARTLY 
BECAUSE OF POLITICAL DEVELOPMENTS LAST FALL." 

THIS WAS AN APPARENT REFERENCE TO THE ABORTIVE UPRISINGS IN HUNGARY 
AND THE POLISH DEMONSTRATIONS LAST YEAR. 

THE REPORT SAID SOVIET COMMITMENTS TO EAST EUROPEAN COUNTRIES CONTI- 
NUE SO LARGE THAT RUSSIAN EXPORTS TO THE WEST ARE LIKELY TO BE SMALL 
DURING THE 12 MONTHS AHEAD. 

THE REPORT SAID EASTERN EUROPE HAS FOUND IT NECESSARY TO BUY SUGAR 
FROM CUBA AND GRAIN FROM THE UNITED STATES. THE LATTER BEING WHEAT 
SOLD TO YUGOSLAVIA. THE EAST ALSO HAS IMPORTED FATS AND OILS. 

"THUS, FOR THE TIME BEING, EAST EUROPE APPEARS MORE IMPORTANT AS 
AN OUTLET FOR FOOD EXPORTING COUNTRIES IN THE WEST THAN AS A COMPETI- 
TOR IN WEST EUROPEAN MARKETS." THE DEPARTMENT ADDED. 

THE REPORT NOTED THAT SINCE THE UPRISINGS IN POLAND AND HUNGARY 
LAST YEAR, GOVERNMENTS HAVE SOUGHT TO RAISE FOOD STANDARDS OF THEIR 
PEOPLES. ‘THEY ALSO HAVE RELAXED COMPULSORY FOOD DELIVERY QUOTAS IMPOSED

WHAT SEEMS TO BE SIGNIFICANT ABOUT THE KHRUSHCHEV GROUP’S DECISION 
ON MALENKOV’S FUTURE IS THAT HE IS BEING GIVEN ANOTHER JOB, HOWEVER 
UNIMPORTANT. AND HE IS NOT _ BEING EXECUTED. 

THE EXPERTS RELATE THIS TO THE GENERAL LINE OF KHRUSHCHEV'S POLICY, 
WHICH SEEMS TO REQUIRE A BELIEF ON THE PART OF THE SOVIET PEOPLE 
GENERALLY THAT THE PENALTY FOR ERROR IN THE SOVIET UNION WILL NO LONGER 
BE EXCESSIVE--THAT FAILURE WILL NOT MEAN DEATH. 

SUCH A BELIEF IS CONSIDERED ESPECIALLY IMPORTANT ON THE PART OF THE 
THOUSANDS OF LOWER LEVEL LEADERS, INDUSTRIAL MANAGERS AND TECHNICIANS. 

THIS IS REGARDED AS TREMENDOUSLY IMPORTANT TO KHRUSHCHEV"S WHOLE 
EFFORT TO INSPIRE THE COUNTRY TO NEW PEAKS OF INDUSTRIAL AND AGRICUL- 
TURAL PRODUCTION BY MEANS WHICH CALL ESSENTIALLY FOR VOLUNTARY RATHER 
THAN FOR FORCED LABOR, 

THE COMMUNIST PARTY BOSS SEEMS TO HAVE DECIDED LONG AGO THAT THE 
COMPULSORY METHODS AND HIGHLY CENTRALIZED CONTROLS DEVELOPED IN 
STALIN'S DAY ARE NOT SUITABLE OR EFFECTIVE FOR AN ERA IN WHICH THE 
SOVIET UNION MUST COMPETE WITH THE FREE NATIONS PRIMARILY IN THE 
ECONOMIC AND POLITICAL FIELDS.

THE SOVIET HISTORY OF BLOODY REPRESSION, TREACHERY, BETRAYAL AND

BY ANY MORAL STANDARDS EXCEPT THE COMMUNIST, THE CURRENT PARTY 
BOSS, NIKITA KHRUSHCHEV, AND THE PRESENT PREMIER, NIKOLAL BULGANIN 
SHOULD HAVE BEEN ETERNALLY GRATEFUL TO KAGANOVICH. AS IRON COMMISSAR 
OF THE UKRAINE, HE STARTED KHRUSHCHEV ON HIS WAY TO THE TOP. AS BOSS OF 
MOSCOW, HE RAISED BULGANIN OUT OF OBSCURITY. 

FOR YEARS, SURVIVING PURGE AFTER PURGE, KAGANOVICH WAS THE 
HIGHEST-RANKING JEW IN THE SOVIET UNION AND THE ONLY ONE IN THE TOP 
RULING GROUP OF THE COMMUNIST PARTY. BUT HE WAS A JEW-HATING JEW, 

WHO CONCURRED IN STALIN'S PERSECUTIONS OF THEM. 

-YET, FOR ALL HIS EXCESSES IN THE NAME OF "BUILDING SOCIALISM," 
KAGANOVICH PROBABLY DID AS MUCH FOR THE STRUGGLING UeSeSeRe AS ANY 
OTHER ONE MAN. HE WAS STALIN'S FAITHFUL SERVANT, ONE OF THE FEW OLD 
BOLSHEVIKS TO SURVIVE THE MASTER'S BLOOD PURGES. SHREWD, ABLE AND 
HARD AS NAILS, HE WAS ALMOST A POLITICAL CARBON COPY OF AIS BOSS.

EXPEDIENT TO PURGE HIM.

PON AULY tap )TuE UNITED STATES REFUSED TO YIELD TODAY 
IN ITS DEMAND THAT ANY INITIAL PERIOD FOR THE SUSPENSION OF HYDROGEN 
BOMB TESTS BE LIMITED TO 10 MONTHS. 

HAROLD Ee STASSEN TOLD THE UeNe DISARMAMENT SUBCOMMITTEE IT WAS 
NOT A QUESTION OF CHOOSING BETWEEN 10 MONTHS AND A SUSPENSION OF TWO 
TO THREE YEARS, AS RUSSIA HAD DEMANDED. THE CHOICE, STASSEN SAID, IS 
BETWEEN A 10-MONTH SUSPENSION OR NO SUSPENSION AT ALL. 

STASSEN, WHO PREVIOUSLY HAD BEEN CHALLENGED BY SOVIET 
DELEGATE VALERIAN ZORIN TO "SHOW US YOUR ARGUMENTS,® LISTED A NUMBER 
OF POINTS TO BACK UP HIS CLAIM THAT THE INITIAL SUSPENSION SHOULD 
BE FOR THE 10-MONTH PERIOD. 

HE SAID THE SHORTER PERIOD WOULD BE LESS CONTROVERSIAL AND 
WOULD HAVE A BETTER CHANCE OF ACCEPTANCE BY A LARGE NUMBER OF 
COVERNMENTS. HE SAID IT WOULD OFFER A FAIR TEST OF THE INTENTIONS 
OF EITHER SIDE TOWARD HALTING THE HYDROGEN BOMB RACE. HE HINTED IT 
WOULD NOT BE SO LONG AS TO ENDANGER EITHER SIDE. 

WESTERN REPRESENTATIVES WHO ATTENDED THE CLOSED MEETING OF THE 
5&lt;-NATION SUBCOMMITTEE DIFFERED WIDELY IN THEIR APPRAISAL OF ZORIN'S 
REACTION. 

MOSCOW RADIO SEIZED ON THE SEEMING DIVISION AMONG THE FOUR 
WESTERN DELEGATIONS AND IN A BROADCAST TONIGHT CHARGED THAT *"EVERY- 
ONE WHO KEEPS TRACK OF THE TALKS CAN SEE PLAINLY THAT THE WESTERN 
REPRESENTATIVES DON'T WANT TO. SETTLE THE DISARMAMENT PROBLEM." 

A COMMENTATOR CLAIMED THAT ALTHOUGH THE WEST HAD AGREED TO A 
SUSPENSION OF NUCLEAR TESTS "THEY COUPLED THEIR AGREEMENT WITH 
RESERVATIONS THAT THROW IT TWO STEPS BACKWARD AND REDUCE THAT 
AGREEMENT TO NOTHING.® 

ZORIN NEITHER ACCEPTED NOR REJECTED STASSEN*S ARGUMENTS. HE SAID 
A FIRST IMPRESSION WAS THAT ALL BUT ONE OF THE POINTS STASSEN LISTED 
COULD BE USED TO SUPPORT A TWO TO THREE YEAR SUSPENSION JUST AS WELL 
AS THE SHORTER PERIOD. HE THEN ADDED HE WOULD STUDY THE STATEMENT 
CAREFULLY AND REPLY LATER.

VE ORMeWY LL CAP I“THE JET AGE IS OPENING UP NEW VISTAS FOR 

i - S LONG BEEN USED BY MILLIONS OF 

WOMEN FOR SCRUBBING POTS AND PANS AND WASHINGTON CLOTHES. 

ITS NEWEST ASSIGNMENT: HELPING TO HURL JET BOMBERS NONSTOP OVER 
DISTANCES NEVER BEFORE ATTAINED WITHOUT REFUELING. 

ITS NAME IS BORAX. ITS BASIC ELEMENT, THE WONDER METAL BORON, 

IS THE MAGIC INGREDIENT IN A NEW JET FUEL THAT CAN INCREASE THE 
RANGE OF HIGH-FLYING BOMBERS BY AS MUCH AS 40 PER CENT. 

IT WILL BE USED IN GUIDED MISSILES. IT WILL POWER THE AIR 
FORCE'S NEW B-58 JET BOMBER WHICH CAN FLY ABOUT TWICE AS FAST AS 
THE SPEED OF SOUND. AT SOME LATER DATE IT MAY BE USED BY COMMERCIAL 
PLANES WHERE INCREASED RANGE, REDUCED FUEL WEIGHT AND INCREASED 
PAYLOAD ARE MAJOR FACTORS. 

BECAUSE OF MILITARY SECURITY CONSIDERATIONS, MANY OF THE FACTS 
ABOUT THE NEW JET FUEL ARE SHROUDED IN SECRECY. SOME INFORMATION 
HAS BEEN DISCLOSED, HOWEVER, BY THE MANUFACTURER--OLIN MATHIESON 
CHEMICAL CORPe--AND BY SPOKESMEN FOR THE U.S. AIR FORCE. 

ITS NAME IS "HEF-2" (THE THREE LETTERS STAND FOR "HIGH 
ENERGY FUEL." EXPECTATIONS ARE THAT IT WILL ADD TERRIFIC PUNCH 
TO THE STRIKING POWER OF THE NATION'S AIR ARM. IT ALSO IS SAID 
TO HAVE A TREMENDOUS POTENTIAL IN CIVILIAN AIRCRAFT. WeCe FOSTER 
EXECUTIVE VICE PRESIDENT OF OLIN MATHIESON, SAYS THE BORON FUEL MAY 
WELL BE THE FORERUNNER OF A NEW INDUSTRY THAT WILL GROSS ONE 
BILLION DOLLARS ANNUALLY WITHIN THE NEXT 10 YEARS. 

HEF-2 IS A CHEMICAL COMPOUND CONTAINING BOTH HYDROGEN AND BORON 
--TWO OF THE HOTTEST-BURNING CHEMICAL ELEMENTS KNOWN TO MAN. BESIDES 
BURNING AT A FIERCE HEAT, BORON PERFORMS THE ADDITIONAL FUNCTION OF 


— me or 


ACTING AS A STABILIZER. “IN ITS PURE STATE, FAST-BURNING HYDROGEN IS 


DIFFICULT TO STORE AND WELL-NIGH IMPOSSIBLE TO CONTROL UNDER CONDI- 
TIONS REQUIRED FOR JET AIRCRAFT PROPULSION. COMBINED WITH 

BORON, AND CERTAIN OTHER CHEMICALS, IT IS SAFE AND EASY TO HANDLE. 
HEF“2) WHICH IS BURNED LIKE ANY OTHER JET FUEL, LOOKS LIKE AN. 

OLIN MATHIESON SCIENTISTS SAY HEF-2, WHEN BURNED, PRODUCES HEAT 
AT THE RATE OF 25,000 BRITISH THERMAL UNITS PER POUND. THIS 
COMPARES WITH 18,500 BTU'S PER POUND FOR CONVENTIONAL AVIATION 

: 

THIS ADDED HEAT INCREASES THE THRUST, OR PROPELLING POWER, OF THE 
FUEL. IT INCREASES THE DISTANCE THAT CAN BE FLOWN WITHOUT REFUELING. 
IT INCREASES SPEED. IT MAKES IT POSSIBLE FOR A CIVILIAN OR TRANSPORT 
PLANE TO CARRY A BIGGER PAYLOAD. "a 


B90 (Q) 

ON THE QUESTION OF RANGE, ALL THAT OLIN MATHIESON WILL SAY 
OFFICIALLY IS THAT "AIR-BREATHING ENGINES CSING MOST ADVANCED HICH- 
ENERGY FUELS HAVE THEIR RANGE INCREASED BY 40 PER CENT. IN CASES 
WHERE RANGE IS NOT THE CONSIDERATION, THEN LESS FUEL FOR A GIVEN 
DISTANCE ALLOWS A GREATER PAYLOAD OR, WITH A CONVENTIONAL PAYLOAD, 
GREATER SPEED." 

IT IS ALSO CLAIMED THAT JETS USING BORON FUEL WILL NOT CONK OUT 
WHEN FLYING AT HIGH ALTITUDES WHERE THE AMOUNT OF OXYGEN IN THE 
ATMOSPHERE IS RELATIVELY SMALLe THIS ENGINE FAILURE AT HIGH 
ALTITUDES IS KNOWN AS "FLAME-OUT" BECAUSE THE FLAME IN THE 
ENGINE DIES OUT. IN A JET PLANE, THE PILOT HAS NO OTHER CHOICE 
BUT TO BAIL OUT OR ATTEMPT A CRASH LANDING. 

BRIG. GENe CeHe MITCHELL, DEPUTY DIRECTOR OF PRODUCTION AT 
WRIGHT PATTERSON AIR FORCE BASE, DAYTON, OHIO, SAYS HE CAN 
VISUALIZE THE USE OF HEF-2 IN THE NOT-TOO-DISTANT FUTURE FOR 
TRANSPORTING CIVILIANS NONSTOP FROM ONE GIVEN POINT TO ANOTHER OVER 
DISTANCES HERETOFORE CONSIDERED IMPOSSIBLE. TRAVEL TIME WILL BE 
SHORTENED, HE SAID, AS JET ENGINES BECOME ABLE TO FUNCTION 
EFFICIENTLY AT HIGH ALTITUDES WHERE THERE IS LITTLE WIND 


RESISTANCE.

PRESIDENT EISENHOWER, BEFORE HE LEFT WASHINGTON, HAD IN THEORY 
SET UP A STATE OF NATIONAL EMERGENCY, ALERTED MILITARY AND CIVIL 
DEFENSE UNITS, AND CREATED A WAR AGENCY TO SUPERVISE PRICE, WAGE, 
RATIONING AND’MANPOWER CONTROLS. 

YESTERDAY'S FIRST PHASE OF THE TEST WAS TO CHECK CIVIL DEFENSE 
ON THE LOCAL LEVEL AND TO REMIND CIVILIANS OF THE NEED TO TAKE 
COVER. THIS EXERCISE WILL LAST THREE DAYS, ALTHOUGH PUBLIC 
PARTICIPATION WAS LIMITED TO ONLY 15 MINUTES. -

BY RICHARD KASISCHKE 

VIENNA, AUSTRIA, JULY 12 CAP)-NIKITA KHRUSHCHEV AND PREMIER © 
BULGANIN LAUNCHED k THREE-DAY TOUR OF THE CZECH PROVINCES TODAY. 
THEIR FIRST STOP WAS IN BRATISLAVA, WHERE KHRUSHCHEV CALLED UPON 
THE RESTIVE SLOVAKS TO COOPERATE WITH THE RED REGIME IN PRAGUE. 

NO WESTERN REPORTERS WERE PERMITTED TO ACCOMPANY THE SOVIET 
LEADERS ON THEIR *®GOODWILL® TOUR INTO THE COUNTRY. BULGANIN AND 
KHRUSHCHEV ARE EXPECTED TO RETURN TO PRAGUE ON SUNDAY. 

PRAGUE RADIO REPORTED ON THEIR ARRIVAL IN og Sh WHERE THEY 
WERE WELCOMED BY KAROL BACILEK, FIRST SECRETARY OF THE SLOVAK COM- 
MUNIST PARTYe 

BACILEK PLEDGED COMPLETE LOYALTY TO THE SOVIET LEADERS AND HAILED 
KHURSHCHEV FOR THE PURGING OF THE *ANTI-PARTY® GROUP IN THE KREMLIN 
LED BY GEORGI MALENKOV, VeJe MOLOTOV AND LAZAR _KAGANOVICH. 

THERE HAD BEEN REPORTS BACILEK MIGHT BE IN DISFAVOR AND FEUDING 
WITH THE CZECHS BECAUSE HE AHD FAILED TO APPEAR IN PRAGUE, FOR THE 
WEDNESDAY AND THURSDAY CONFERENCES WITH THE MOSCOW CHIEFS. INQUIRIES 
BROUGHT THE RT Me HE WAS NOT WELL. BUT BACILEK APPEARED IN 
GOOD HEALTHY VOIC ° 

BACILEK HAS BEEN REPORTED AT ODDS WITH THE PRAGUE COMMUNIST 
CHIEFS OVER SLOVAKKIA*S PERSISTENT DEMAND FOR AUTONOMY WITHIN THE 
CZECHOSLOVAK STATE -- A STATUS WHICH THE SLOVAKS HAD DURING THE GER- 
MAN OCCUPATION OF WORLD WAR II. THE STAUNCHLY INDEPENDENT AND 
PREDOMINANTLY CATHOLIC SLOVAKS STILL NURSE RESENTMENT AGAINST 
CZECHS WHO CONTROL THE COUNTRY AND MONOPOLIZE THE GOVERNMENT JOBS 
FROM PRAGUE. 

IT WAS BELIEVED KHRUSHCHEV AND BULGANIN CHOSE BRATISLAVA FOR THE 
FIRST STOP IN ORDER TO APPEASE THE SLOVAKS AND TRY TO GET THEM WORKING 
IN CLOSER HARMONY WITH PRAGUE. 


IN HIS SPEECH AT BRATISLAVA, KHRUSHCHEV URGED THE SLOVAKS *TO 
RECOGNIZE THE BROTHERLY AID OF THE CZECHS." 

*SLOVAKIA WAS A POOR COUNTRY AND RANKED AMONG THE MOST BACKWARD 
IN EUROPE, FORCING MANY SLOVAKS TO LEAVE THEIR HOMES IN ORDER TO 
SEEK THEIR BREAD ABROAD® HE SAID. HE ASSERTED THE COMMUNIST 
REGINE HAD BROUGHT ABOUT A FAST CHANGE IN THIS RESPECT. 

WITH THE SETTING UP OF NEW FACTORIES AND THE MODERNIZATION OF 
SLOVAKIA’S AGRICULTURE THE WAY TO A BETTER LIFE HAS BEEN PAVED 

KHRUSHCHEV URGED BOTH SLOVAKS AND CZECHS TO COLLABORATE IN t 
SPIRIT OF FRIENDSHIP. 

TURNING TO INTERNATIONAL MATTERS, KHRUSHCHEV ACCUSED THE 
WESTERN POWERS OF HAMPERING THE LONDON DISARMAMENT TALKS BY ®TYING 
THEN UP WITH THE ENTIRELY SEPARATE QUESTION OF THE REUNIFICATION 

KHRUSHCHEV WAS FREQUENTLY INTERRUPTED BY APPLAUSE, ALTHOUGH HIS 
SPEECH WAS NOT TRANSLATED INTO SLOVAK. HE DECLARED: 

RELATIONS BETWEEN SOCIALIST COUNTRIES ARE BASED ON THE PRINCIPLES 
OF FULL EQUALITY AND SOVEREIGNTY. 

THE IMPERIALISTS SHAMELESSLY TRY TO REPRESENT THEMSELVES AS 
THE LIBERATORS OF EUROPE. BUT TODAY THEY ARM THE GERMAN MILI-

CHANGED SIGNALS AND DECIDED TO LET AVERY BRUNDAGE TRAVEL TO COMMUNIST 
BULGARIA FOR A MEETING OF THE INTERNATIONAL OLYMPICS COMMITTEE WHICH 

NOW, STATE DEPARTMENT OFFICIALS ARE TRYING TO DECIDE HOW TO CARRY 
OUT THE POLICY. 

THE HEART OF THEIR PROBLEM IS TO ANNOUNCE IT IN SUCH A MANNER THAT 
THEY WILL NOT BE LETTING DOWN THE BARS GENERALLY AGAINST TRAVEL TO 
BULGARIA BY THE DECISION TO LET BRUNDAGE MAKE THE TRIP.

BRUNDAGE WOULD BE ALLOWED TO GO ARE ®PREMATURE.® THIS IS THE KIND OF 
REACTION USUAL IN CASES WHERE A DECISION HAS BEEN MADE BUT BEFORE IT 
IS PUT IN SHAPE FOR ANNOUNCEMENT.

(400) CHINA TRADE BUDGET 
BY JOHN SCALI 

WASHINGTON. JULY 14 (AP)-THE ‘UNITED STATES RESUMES ITS FIGHT THIS 
WEFK TO KEEP WESTERN TRADE WITH COMMUNIST CHINA AT A BARE MINIMUM. 

A BACKSTAGE ARGUMENT WITH BRITAIN, FRANCE, WEST GERMANY AND JAPAN 
SEEMS LIKELY TO DEVELOP IN A NEW ROUND OF TALKS SET TO OPEN IN PARIS 
AMONG REPRESENTATIVES OF 15 KEY TRADING COUNTRIES. 

THE ISSUE WILL BE HOW BIG A QUOTA TO SET FOR SOME 25 IMPORTANT 
TRADE ITEMS WHICH PREVIOUSLY WERE BANNED FROM SHIPMENT TO RED CHINA. 

THE AMERICAN DELEGATION HAS BEEN INSTRUCTED TO FIGHT FOR THE LOWEST 
POSSIBLE QUOTA. BRITAIN. WHICH IS LEADING THE BATTLE TO EASE CHINA 
TRADE CONTROLS. CAN BE EXPECTED TO DEMAND BIGGER QUOTAS THAN THE 
UNITED STATES WOULD LIKE.

THE EISENHOWER ADMINISTRATION LOST A BIG ROUND MAY 30 IN ITS STRUG- 
GLE TO KEEP ECONOMIC PRESSURE ON THE PEIPING GOVERNMENT. 

ON THAT DAY BRITAIN ANNOUNCED THAT DESPITE STRENUOUS AMERICAN OBJEC- 
TIONS IT PROPOSED TO BEGIN SHIPPING 207 ITEMS BARRED FROM CHINA TRADE 
SINCE THE KOREAN WAR. 

@ANY OTHER WESTERN COUNTRIES, FEARING BRITAIN WOULD GET A COMPETI- 
TIVE JUMP IN THE CHINA MAINLAND MARKET, HAVE DECIDED SINCE TO FOLLOW 
BRITAIN’S EXAMPLE. 

THE 15-NATION TALKS WHICH ARE TO BEGIN IN PARIS EARLY THIS WEEK 
WILL DEAL WITH A SECOND BRITISH DEMAND--THAT QUOTAS BE SET FOR 25 
EVEN MORE IMPORTANT TRADE ITEMS WHICH HAVE BEEN ON THE EMBARGO LIST. 
QUOTAS TO BE AGREED UPON WILL COVER ONLY THE REMAINDER OF THIS YEAR 
MAKING IT LIKELY THE FIGHT WILL BE RENEWED WHEN PLANS FOR 1958 TRADE 
COME UP FOR DISCUSSION LATER. 

STATE DEPARTMENT OFFICIALS FEAR THAT JAPAN, WHICH PREVIOUSLY STEERED 
A MIDDLE GROUND POSITION BETWEEN CONFLICTING BRITISH AND AMERICAN VIEW- 
POINTS, THIS TIME MAY SWING OVER TO BRITAIN'S SIDE, ARGUING HER ECONO- 
MIC LIVELIHOOD DEMANDS MORE TRADE WITH THE CHINA MAINLAND. | 

JAPAN'S PRIME MINISTER KISHI DURING HIS TALKS WITH PRESIDENT EISEN- 
MOWER LAST MONTH FRANKLY SAID HIS GOVERNMENT FAVORED MORE SUCH TRADE 
BUT ONLY.IN COMMODITIES WHICH WOULD NOT -BE APT-TO INCREASE RED- 
CHINA’S WAR MAKING POTENTIAL. 

AT PRESENT, WESTERN NATIONS THROUGH A COMMITTEE IN PARIS MAINTAIN 
THREE SEPARATE TRADE LISTS TO GUIDE COMMERCE WITH THE COMMUNIST BLOC. 
THE FIRST, COVERING 160 ITEMS, IS THE SO CALLED "TOTAL EMBARGO" LIST. 
THE SECOND, WHICH WILL BE DISCUSSED AT PARIS, COVERS 25 ITEMS 
WHICH CAN BE SHIPPED ONLY IN LIMITED NUMBERS. A THIRD IS CALLED THE 
®WATCH LIST® WHICH CONSISTS OF ITEMS WHICH CAN BE SHIPPED WITHOUT 
RESTRICTION PROVIDING THE REDS DO NOT BUY TOO MUCH OF ANY ONE. 

COUNTRIES WHICH WILL DISCUSS THE NWEST PHASE OF THE CHINA TRADE 
PROBLEM ARE THE UNITED STATES, BRITAIN, FRANCE, WEST GERMANY, CANADA, 
ITALY, BELGIUM, THE NETHERLANDS, LUXEMBOURG, DENMARK, NORWAY, GREECE, 
TURKEY» PORTUGAL AND JAPAN.

THE TERMS OF THE DRAFT AND LOWER THE DRAFT AGE. ALTHOUGH CONGRESS | 
PASSED THE TRAINING: PROGRAM, THE FIRST TIME SUCH A PROPOSAL HAD 
SUCCEEDED IN RECEIVING CONGRESSIONAL SANCTION, THE LEGISLATORS SUB- 
SEQUENTLY FAILED TO ENACT SUPPORTING PROVISIONS TO PUT THE PROGRAM 
INTO OPERATION. 

THE COMMISSION THEN WAS ASSIGNED THE ROLE OF OVERSEEING JOB OF OVER- 
HAULING AND MODERNIZING THE RESERVE PROGRAMS OF THE ARMED FORCES,

NOT BY CIVILIANS BUT BY THE MILITARY. THIS BEING SO, I MUST CON- 
CLUDE THAT CONTINUED OPERATION OF THE COMMISSION IN EXISTING CIR- 
CUMSTANCES, AND IN THE FACE OF APPARENT CONGRESSIONAL DISINCLINATION

BOMBAY, INDIA, JULY 14 (AP)-PRIME MINISTER NEHRU CAME HOME TODAY 
AFTER A MONTE IN EUROPE AND THE MIDDLE EAST. HE TOURED SCANDINAVIA 4 
ATTENDED THE COMMONWEALTH CONFERENCE IN LONDON AND HAS SPENT THE LAST 
THREE DAYS CONFERRING IN CAIRO WITH PRESIDENT NASSER. 

—— ‘- ene — ceeeenee we 860 weww te kl lt Ube WIA WEIVL WHOOLKN e 

THE NEHRU-NASSER TALKS FAILED TO BRING EGYPT AND BRITAIN VISIBILY 
CLOSER TO RESTORATION OF DIPLOMATIC RELATIONS. THESE RELATIONS HAVE 
BEEN BROKEN SINCE THE BRITISH-FRENCH ATTACK ON EGYPT LAST FALL. EGYPT 
HAS SHOWN SOME EAGERNESS TO REPAIR THE BREAK. 

A DISPATCH FROM CAIRO AND NEHRU HAD MADE NO SPECIFIC PROPOSALS, 
BUT GAVE NASSER A RUNDOWN ON THE LONDON ATTITUDE. 

INFORMANTS CLOSE TO BOTH EGYPTIAN AND INDIAN SIDES IN THE TALKS 
SAID NEHRU HAD EMPHASIZED BRITISH INSISTENCE ON COMPENSATION FOR 


MATERIAL SEIZED FROM THE OLD BRITISH MILITARY BASE ON THE SUEZ CANAL. 
AT THE TIME NASSER SAID HE WAS TAKING THE BRITISH STORES TO COMPENSATE 
FOR EGYPTIAN EQUIPMENT DESTROYED BY BRITISH BOMBING. 
THE BRITISH ARE ALSO INSISTING ON FAIR COMPENSATION TO THE 
OLD SUEZ CANAL COs, IN WHICH THE BRITISH GOVERNMENT WAS THE BIGGEST 
SHAREHOLDER, AS WELL AS COMPENSATION TO BRITISH FIRMS WHOSE PROPERTY 
HAS BEEN CONFISCATED BY THE EGYPTIAN GOVERNMENT IN THE LAST FEW MONTHS. 
THE EGYPTIANS WANT TO REGAIN THEIR STERLING BALANCES BLOCKED IN 
LONDON AND TO REVIVE TRADE WITH BRITAIN. THEY ALSO APPEAR TO HOPE 
A RESTORATION OF RELATIONS WOULD COUNTER U.S. INFLUENCE IN THE 
MIDDLE EAST. THEY REGARD THE EISENHOWER DOCTRINE AS ESSENTIALLY 
HOSTILE TO THEM, AND THE OLD EGYPTIAN TACTIC HAS BEEN TO TRY TO 
PLAY ONE WESTERN POWER AGAINST ANOTHER.

SEVEN ASSOCIATES TO GUDOK, VOROBOV SUDDENLY REALIZED HIS SECTION OF THE 
VLADIVOSTOK LINE WAS IN DANGER OF NOT MEETING ITS QUOTA FOR DELIVERIES 
OF LIQUID FREIGHT. 

VOROBOV EAD AN INSPIRATION. HE ORDERED 50 TANK CARS FILLED WITH 
WATER AND SHIPPED FROM VOROSHILMV TO USURISKY. AT USURISKY THE WATER 
FROZE IN THE CARS AND IT TOOK A MONTH TO GET THEM THAWED OUT AND 
EMPTIED. BUT VOROBOV MET HIS QUOTA AND KEPT HIS JOB. 








THIS SUMMER VOROBOV AGAIN FELL BEHIND ON HIS LIQUID DELIVERIES. 
CONSOLED BY THE THOUGHT THAT WATER DOES NOT FREEZE IN SUMMER, HE 
DEVISED AN EVEN BETTER PLAN. HE ORDERED WATER PUMPED FROM MAINS AT 
PERVAYA RECHKA DIRECTLY INTO TANK CARS AND SHIPPED TO EGERSHELD 
NEARBY, WHERE IT COULD BE EMPTIED BACK INTO 
THE MAINS AND ALLOWED TO FLOW BACK TO PERVAYA RECHKA. 

AT THIS RATE, THE WRITERS SAID, VOROBOV COULD FULFILL THE WHOLE 
ANNUAL PLAN IN A MONTH, BUT TO SPEED THINGS UP EVEN MO’: HE SENT 15 
CARS WITH NOTHING BUT AIR. THIS SIMPLIFIED THE UNLOA?.N%, SINCE SOME OF 
THE WATER LET OUT AT EGERSHELD WASHED OUT THE ROADBED A... CAUSED TRAFFIC

HOLLISTER, WHO TOOK OVER HIS JOB TWO YEARS AGO HOPING TO MAKE “SUB- 
STANTIAL REDUCTIONS" IN FOREIGN AID SPENDING, ENDED BY URGING AMERICANS 
TO CONSIDER SUCH AID AS A "PERMANENT PART® OF AMERICAN FOREIGN POLICY 
AS LONG AS COMMUNISM THREATENS THE WORLD. 

HE SUGGESTED THAT AMERICAN DIPLOMATS BE GIVEN INTENSIVE ECONOMIC 
AID TRAINING IN THE FUTURE BECAUSE "THIS IS NO LONGER A YEAR-BY- 

YEAR EMERGENCY." 

HOLLISTER, IN TALKING ABOUT HIS SUCCESSOR, STRONGLY URGED HE ALSO BE 
MADE A "SINGLE DIRECTING HEAD FOR ALL Ue Se ECONOMIC ACTIVITIES IN THE 
FOREIGN FIELDe” HE PROPOSED THAT THIS MAN BE GIVEN THE POWER TO COOR- 
DINATE OPERATIONS BY THE GOVERNMENT'S EXPORT-IMPORT BANK AS WELL AS 
SALES OF SURPLUS FARM PRODUCTS ABROAD. 

A CONSERVATIVE REPUBLICAN OF THE TAFT SCHOOL, HOLLISTER ACKNOWLEDGED 
WITH OUT EMBARRASSMENT THAT HIS FOREIGN AID AGENCY IS SPENDING MORE 
MONEY NOW AND HAS MORE EMPLOYEES THAN WHEN HE TOOK OVER.

ANN ARBOR, MICHe, JULY 16 ~THE BUREMESE AMBASSANOR TO THE 
UNITED STATES DESCRIBED-HTSCOONTRY “POA AS "A SOCIAL DEMOCRATIC 
STATE AND SOCIETY WITH UNIVERSAL SUFFRAGE AND FULL FREEDOM OF RELIGION 
AND CIVIC RIGHTS FOR ALL CITIZENS." 

"BURMA IS AN OPEN SOCIETY IN WHICH ANY PERSON, MALE OR FEMALE, MAY 
“LIMB TO THE HIGHEST RUNG OF THE LADDER THROUGH COMPETENCY," AMBASSADOR 
} WIN (CAPS U, W) DECLARED IN A SPEECH AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN. 

WIN APPEARED AS A GUEST SPEAKER IN THE UNIVERSITY'S SUMMER 
LECTURE PROGRAM. 

"FROM THE BIRTHOF BURMA AS AN INDEPENDENT REPUBLIC AFTER A CENTURY 
AND A QUARTER OF ENGLISH COLONIAL DOMINATION WE RESOLVED TO BECOME 
[THAT KIND OF A DEMOCRATIC SOCIETY WHICH IN THIS COUNTRY WOULD BE 
2EGARDED AS CONFORMING TO THE PRINCIPLES OF CULTURAL PLURALISM," WIN | 

Alle 

"THAT IS," HE SAID, "WE RESPECT THE INTEGRITY OF OUR ETHNIC AND 
RELIGIOUS VARIATIONS {N A COMPLETELY FREE AND OPEN SOCIETY IN WHICH 
ALL MEMBERS HAVE UNIFORM CITIZENSHIP." 

WIN SAID HE THOUGHT THE MOST SIGNIFICANT ASPECT OF BURMESE CULTURAL 
LIFE WAS ITS "PERVASIVENESS." c7 

"IT BELONGS TO THE PEOPLE,” HE SAID. i QES NOT BELONG TO 
A SMALL WESTERN EDUCATED GROUP OR TO A SWALY EDUCATED CLASS ‘ELITE.'" 

®THOUGH PERHAPS NOT ALL THE PEOPLE CAN SHARE IN THE ESOTERIC 
LEARNING OF BUDDHISM OR OF THE OTHER FAITHS OF OUR COUNTRY," WIN 
DECLARED, "NEVERTHELESS, MOST OF THE PEOPLE SOMEHOW CONTRIVE TO SHARE 
IN THE VARIOUS CULTURAL ASPECTS SINCE MANY OF THEM ARE INTEGRAL TO 
THE BURMESE DAILY CALENDER AND SEASONAL LIFE." 

"THE EVER PRESENT VISIT TO THE PAGODA AND MONASTERIES, THE HEARING 
AND TELLING OF STORIES, THE MAKING OF HAND CRAFTED MATERIAL, THE 
SHARING OF ALL THESE CREATE A WIDE SPECTRUM OF CULTURAL AND ESTHETIC 
EXPERIENCE INTEGRAL TO THE LIFE OF THE PEOPLE," THE DIPLOMAT SAID.

MAIN AIM. IT IS THE FIRST MEETING OF THE INSTITUTE IN A RED-RULED 
COUNTRY AND THE FIRST SINCE THE WAR IN WHICK MARXIST PHILOSOPHERS ARE 

THEORETICAL DISCUSSIONS WITH NON-COMMUNISTS COULD HAVE SOME IN- 
FLUENCE ON THE COMMUNISTS, THE WESTERN SOURCES SAID. 

RICHARD MCKEON (CAPS M’K), PROFESSOR OF PHILOSOPHY AT THE UNIVERSITY 
OF CHICAGO, IS THE INSTITUTE’S PRESIDENT. 

THERE WERE ONLY FOUR MEMBERS WITH BEARDS PRESENT AS THE PHILOSO- 
PHERS MET IN THE GREEN AND WHITE MARBLE HALL OF THE POLISH ACADEMY OF 
SCIENCE. AS HOST COUNTRY, POLAND HAS 20 DELEGATES. OTHER NATIONS 
INCLUDE THE UNITED STATES, BRITAIN, FRANCE, WEST GERMANY, CANADA, 

JAPAN, BELGIUM, ITALY AND ALL THE COMMUNIST BLOC COUNTRIES. 

MCKEON SAID’ IN HIS OPENING STATEMENT THE YEARS HAVE SHOWN THAT 
COMMUNICATION AMONG PHILOSOPHERS CANNOT BE ACHIEVED MERELY BY THE EX- 
CHANGE OF DOCUMENTS. IT IS ALSO NECESSARY TO SUBMIT PREFORMED IDEAS 
TO THE TEST OF DISCUSSION, HE SAID. 

THE INCREASE OF NATIONALIST TENDENCIES IN THE LAST 10 YEARS WAS 
TOO SYMPTOMATIC OF RIGIDITY IN THINKING, MCKEON SAID. HE ADDED THAT IF 
EASTERN AND WESTERN PHILOSOPHERS COULD FIND COMMON MEANINGS OF SUCH 
WORDS AS FREEDOM AND TRUTH IT SHOULD BE POSSIBLE FINALLY TO FIND A 
MEASURE OF POLITICAL UNDERSTANDING. 

MC KEON AND PROF.sANDREI SHYSKIN ARE SCHEDULED TO OPEN THE DIScus- 
SION ON THE PHILOSOPHER'S IMPORTANCE IN PRACTICAL LIFE, ONE OF THE 
THREE MAIN TOPICS. THE OTHERS ARE THE RELATION OF THOUGHT AND ACTION, 
AND THE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY OF PHILOSOPHERS. 

PROF eTADEUSZ KOTARABINSKI, PRESIDENT OF THE POLISH ACADEMY OF 
SCIENCE, TOLD THE CONFERENCE HE HOPED WARSAW COULD BECOME A CROSSROADS 
FOR THINKERS "APPLYING DIFFERENT METHODS BUT STRIVING IN COMMON TO 
ARRIVE AT MORALLY VALUABLE SOLUTIONS OF URGENT ISSUES."

E te COMMUNEST WORLD SOUNDS LIKE BAD NEWS TO 
THE AVERAGE CZECH. 


THEY RECALL WHAT NINE YEARS OF HELPING MAINTAIN THE ECONOMY OF 
THE SOVIET UNION AND KEEPING SOME OF THE MORE FALTERING SATELLITES 
ALIVE HAVE DONE TO THIS ONCE PROSPEROUS NATION, 

THE PROMISE FROM KHRUSHCHEV OF GREATER ECONOMIC COOPERATION MEANS 
TO MANY PEOPLE HERE AN EVEN GREATER DRAIN ON A NATION WHOSE LIVING 
STANDARDS HAVE SUFFERED MUCH SINCE IT BECAME COMMUNIST. 

*WE MIGHT ACHIEVE AN EVEN BETTER COORDINATION IN THE WORK OF THE 
INDUSTRY AND AGRICULTURE OF OUR COUNTRIES SO THAT OUR ECONOMY NIGHT BE 
ae _—* LINKED,*® KHRUSHCHEV SAID BEFORE HE LEFT PRAGUE ON 

SDAYe | 

HE SPOKE ALSO OF CZECH FACTORIES WHICH WERE NOT BEING OPERATED AT 
cote og AND OF THE NEED TO RENOVATE OLD FACTORIES BEFORE BUILDING 
MORE NE Se 

TO SOME CZECHS THIS SOUNDED LIKE ANOTHER MOVE TO DRAIN OFF EVEN 
MORE HEAVY INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTS AND CONSUMER GOODS TO STRENGTHEN THE 
COMMUNIST CAMP. 

"WHAT DO WE GET IN RETURN?® ASKED ONE CZECH MAN ON THE STREET. 

"IT LOOKS LIKE ALL WE GET IS THE PROMISE OF SOVIET MILITARY PROTECTION 
FROM POSSIBLE ENEMIES IN EUROPE.®* 

EVEN AFTER NINE YEARS OF CONTRIBUTING TO THE COMMUNIST BUILDUP 
CZECHOSLOVAKIA REMAINS AN ATTRACTIVE PLACE IN COMPARISON TO OTHER 
KREMLIN SATELLITESs 

THE SHOPS OF PRAGUE ARE RELATIVELY WELL FILLED WITH CONSUMER GOODS, 
SOMETHING THE PEOPLE OF RUSSIA SELDOM SEE. PRICES, WHILE HIGH, ARE 
NOT BEYOND THE REACH OF MANY PEOPLE. 

KHRUSHCHEV MUST HAVE NOTICED HOW MUCH BETTER DRESSED ARE PRAGUE’S 
PEOPLE THAN HIS OWN NATIONS, WHO PLOD THROUGH RED SQUARE AND THE 
BROAD AVENUES OF MOSCOW. CZECH MEN AND WOMEN APPEAR FAR AHEAD OF 
THEIR COUNTERPARTS IN RUSSIA IN CLOTHING, FOOD, AND HOUSING, 


MANY CZECHS HERE SAY THEY FEAR KHRUSHCHEV'’S SUGGESTION FOR 
ECONOMIC INTEGRATION IS SIMPLY ANOTHER PLAN TO DRIVE THE CZECH ECONOMY 
DOWN TO THE LEVEL OF RUSSIA AND THE WEAKER SATELLITES. KHRUSHCHEV 
ALLEGED THE WESTERN POWERS ARE THREATENING A TRADE BLOCKADE. 

EXPERIENCED OBSERVERS HERE PREDICTED THERE WOULD BE RESISTANCE, 
PERHAPS EVEN AT GOVERNMENT AND PARTY LEVEL, TO ANY DRASTIC CHANGE IN 
THE CZECH ECONOMY. 

"CZECHOSLOVAKIA TODAY IS NOT STABILIZED, IT IS SIMPLY DORMANT," SAID 
ONE EUROPEAN DIPLOMAT WITH LONG EXPERIENCE HERE. "THERE COULD BE 
TROUBLE IF THE SOVIET UNION TRIES TO TAKE AWAY FROM THE PEOPLE OF THIS 
COUNTRY WHAT THEY HAVE LEFT.® 

HE SAID HE BELIEVED CZECHOSLOVAKIA’S COMMUNIST RULERS WERE AWARE 
OF THAT POSSIBILITY AND WHILE THEY WOULD AGREE TO GREATER ECONOMIC 
COOPERATION WITH THE SOVIET UNION THEY WOULD PLEAD WITH THE KREMLIN TO 
GO SLOW ON ANY DRASTIC CHANGES. 3 

HOUSING, WHILE A PROBLEM IN PRAGUE AND ELSEWHERE IN CZECHOSLOVAKIA, 
IS BY NO MEANS THE CRITICAL SITUATION IT IS IN RUSSIA. 

MOST PEOPLE HERE AT LEAST MANAGE PRIVATE THOUGH SMALL QUARTERS. 

THE GOVERNMENT HAS DEVOTED A REASONABLE PORTION OF EXPENDITURES TO 
HOUSING AND CONSUMER GOODS. 

PRAGUE AND ITS SISTER CITIES ARE STILL FILLED WITH BEER HALLS AND 
SIMILAR PLACES OF ENTERTAINMENT. WORKERS, EVEN FACTORY HANDS OF THE 
LOWEST LEVEL, MANAGE THEIR TALL STEINS OF BEER, THEIR MUSIC, AND 
THEIR DANCING FREQUENTLY. 

IF WE HAVE TO GIVE MORE TO THE SOVIET UNION IT COULD MEAN CUTTING 
INTO THAT TRADITIONAL LIFE WE ENJOY," SAID ONE CZECH. "I DON’T THINK 
OUR LEADERS ARE FOOLISH ENOUGH TO PERMIT THAT.®

MOST OF THE REPORTS HAVE ONE THING IN COMMON. THEY TELL OF 
TROUBLE THE CHINESE COMMUNISTS ARE HAVING IN CLINCHING THEIR HOLD ON 
TIBET, SEVEN YEARS AFTER RED TROOPS MARCHED INTO THE COUNTRY. 

IN THE KALIMPONG-DARJEELING AREA OF NORTHEASTERN INDIA A USUALLY 
RELIABLE SOURCE REPORTS THAT CHINESE PLANES DROPPED AN UNUSUAL KIND 
OF BOMBS ON REBEL KHAMPA TRIBESMEN IN NORTHEASTERN TIBETe FREQUENT 
REPORTS OF CLASHES BETWEEN THE WARLIKE KHAMPAS AND CHINESE TROOPS HAVE 
COME OUT OF TIBET EVER SINCE THE CHINESE INVASION. 

SPORADIC BOMBINGS, ACCORDING TO THIS SOURCE, TOOK PLACE IN THE 
KHAM AREA ABOUT 150 MILES FROM LHASA FROM LATE DECEMBER TO THE END OF 
LAST FEBRUARY. THIS SOURCE SAID SMOKE FROM THE BOMBS CAUSED PAINFUL 
SKIN IRRITATIONS ALL OVER THE BODY, FOLLOWED BY INTENSE 
STOMACH PAINS, AND THAT APPARENTLY MANY PERSONS DIED. 

THE INDIAN FOREIGN MINISTRY IN NEW DELHI SAID THERE WERE REPORTS 
FROM TIME TO TIME OF FIGHTING IN THE KHAM AREA, BUT A SPOKESMAN DE- 
CLINED TO GIVE AN EVALUATION OF THE BOMBING REPORT. 

ANOTHER REPORT OF TIBETAN REBEL ACTION AGAINST THEIR CHINESE RULERS 
CAME FROM KATMANDU, CAPITAL OF THE MOUNTAIN KINGDOM OF NEPAL LYING 
BETWEEN TIBET AND INDIA. A PERSON WITH ACCESS TO OFFICIAL NEPALESE 
INFORMATION SAID THAT AN ATTEMPT WAS MADE ON THE LIFE OF A CHINESE

®THIS WOULD NEITHER BE REAL DISARMAMENT NOR CONDUCIVE TO

RATIFICATION TODAY OF THE TREATIES CREATING A SIX-NATION EUROPEAN

RATIFICATION PROCESS IS SCHEDULED TO BE COMPLETED BY THE END OF THIS

APPROVAL THIS FALLe

TREATY PROVIDES FOR THE PROGRESSIVE ELIMINATION OF TARIFFS WITHIN THE

MANILA, JULY 19 (AP)-THE UsSe EMBASSY TODAY ADVISED THE 
PHILIPPINE GOVERNMENT IT CANNOT TAKE STEPS TO HAVE A FORMER NAVY 
MAN RETURNED TO THIS COUNTRY TO FACE A PENDING CRIMINAL CHARGE. 

THE EMBASSY ALSO REJECTED A PHILIPPINE GOVERNMENT REQUEST 
THAT AN AIR FORCE STAFF SERGEANT BE BROUGHT BACK FOR TRIAL IN AN 
AUTOMOBILE ACCIDENT CASE. 

THE UNITED STATES POSITION WAS CONTAINED IN TWO NOTES SENT 
TO THE GOVERNMENT OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS. 

ONE NOTE COVERED THE CASE OF GEORGE E. ROE, OF CLIO, MICH. 
FORMERLY STATIONED HERE WITH THE NAVY. IMINAL COMPLAINT WAS 
FILED AGAINST ROE IN CONNECTION WITH AN AUTOMOBILE ACCIDENT ON 


JANe 15 19566 
THE OTHER NOTE CONCERNED AIR FORCE STAFF SERGEANT ROY 0. 


COOK WHO WAS CHARGED WITH DAMAGES TO PROPERTY THROUGH RECKLESS 
IMPRUDENCE AS THE RESULT OF AN AUTOMOBILE ACCIDENT ON JAN. 1) 1956. 
IN THE ROE CASE, THE EMBASSY POINTED OUT THAT IT WAS NOT 
KNOWN ROE WOULD BE WANTED TO STAND TRIAL UNTIL AFTER HE HAD BEEN 

RETURNED TO THE UNITED STATES AND RECEIVED HIS DISCHARGE. 

IT IS, THEREFORE, IMPOSSIBLE TO RETURN HIM TO THE PHILIPPINES 
SINCE THERE-IS -NO--EXTRADITION TREATY BETWEEN. THE.UNITED-STATES AND 
THE PHILIPPINES.» 

THE EMBASSY POINTED OUT THAT THE PRELIMINARY INVESTIGATION IN 
ROE'S CASE "EXTENDED OVER A PERIOD OF EIGHT AND ONE-HALF MONTHS 
AND THIS LONG DELAY UNDOUBTEDLY CONTRIBUTED TO THE 
INADVERTENT TRANSFER OF ROE. THIS DELAY WAS PARTICULARLY LONG 
IN VIEW OF THE UNAGGRAVATED NATURE OF THE OFFENSE WITH WHICH ROE 
WAS SUBSEQUENTLY CHARGED, WHICH IS PUNISHABLE BY A MAXIMUM 
SENTENCE OF FOUR MONTHS® CONFINEMENT,

THAT THE DEPARTMENT HAS WAITED UNTIL MID-1957 TO BRING TO OUR

OVER A YEAR AND A HALF AGO AND WITH RESPECT TO SERVICEMEN 
TRANSFERRED A YEAR AGO."

MAEBAGHI&gt;  TAPAK JULY 19 (AP 

(AP)-WILLIAM GIRARD'S ARMY AND JAPANESE 
LEGAL ADVISERS AGREED TODAY TO FOREGO FURTHER HELP FROM AMERICAN 
CIVILIAN ATTORNEYS IN DEFENDING THE YOUNG CI FROM A MANSLAUGHTER 

WITH THE ARMY ADVISERS* CONSENT, JAPANESE LAWYER ITSURO HAYASHI 
ASSUMED OVER-ALL DIRECTION OF GIRARD’S DEFENSE IN HIS TRIAL SCHEDULED 
FOR AUG. 26 IN A JAPANESE COURT HERE. AT THE SUGGESTION OF HIS BROTHER 
IN THE UNITED STATES, GIRARD ONCE TRIED TO FIRE HAYASHI. 

THE WELL KNOWN JAPANESE ATTORNEY MAPPED PLANSS FOR THE DEFENSE WITH 
MAJ. STANLEY LEVIN AND BRIG. CEN. CHARLES DECKER, THE ARMY'S ASSISTANT 
JUDGE ADVOCATE GENERAL WHO WAS ASSIGNED TO SEE THAT GIRARD'S RIGHTS 
WERE SAFEGUARDED. HAYASHI ALSO MET WITH THE CHIEF JUDGE OF THE

WASHINGTON, JULY 20-(AP)-PRESIDENT EISENHOWER LET CONGRESS KNOW 
TODAY HE LOOK’ WITH STRONG DISFAVOR ON LEGISLATION WHICH WOULD KILL OFF 
OR DRASTICALLY CURB THIS COUNTRY’S STATUS-OF-FORCE TREATIES WITH 
ALLIED NATIONS. THESE TREATIES AND AGREEMENTS PROVIDE FOR FOREIGN 
COURT TRIAL OF AMERICAN SERVICEMEN CHARGED WITH ‘VIOLATION OF CIVIL LAWS 

IN A LETTER REPLY TO AN INQUIRY FROM REP. MARTIN OF MASSACHUSETTS, 
REPUBLICAN LEADER IN THE HOUSE, EISENHOWER SAID: 

1. PASSAGE OF ANY SUCH LEGISLATION WOULD BE °MOST HURTFUL," WOULD 
*CRAVELY THREATEN” NATIONAL SECURITY, “ALIENATE OUR FRIENDS" AND °CIVE 
COMFORT TO THOSE SHO WANT TO DESTROY OUR WAY OF LIFE.® 

&gt;. THE UNITED STATES SHOULD NOT DEMAND SPECIAL PRIVILEGES--*EXTRA- 
TERRITORIALITY®--BY WHICH NATIONS WHERE Ue Se FORCES ARE STATIONED 
WOULD SURRENDER THEIR RIGHT OF SOVEREIGNTY OVER OFFENSES COMMITTED IN 
THEIR TERRITORY. 

3. THIS QUESTION IS ®NO PARTISAN POLITICAL MATTER." 

MOVES TO STRIKE OUT OR CHANGE THE STATUS-OF-FORCES AGREEMENTS WERE 
ACCELERATED BY THE SUPREME COURT DECISION IN THE GIRARD CASE. THE 
COURT RULED THAT THE JAPANESE GOVERNMENT SHOULD BE PERMITTED TO TRY GI 
WILLIAM Se CIRARD ON THE CHARGE THAT HE SHOT AND KILLED A JAPANESE 
WOMAN WHO WAS PICKING UP EMPTY SHELLS ON AN AMERICAN FIRING RANGE

BY KENNETH WHITING 

(ADVANCE FOR USE IN AMS SUNDAY, JULY 21 1957) 

(ADVANCE) CHICAGO, JULY 20 (APS-HANDICRAFTS -- THE UBIQUITOUS 
ATTRACTION FOR TOURISTS AND VACATIONERS THROUGHOUT THE WORLD --HAS 
BECOME A LITTLE-KNOWN PART OF THE VAST AMERICAN FOREIGN AID 

SINCE THE PROGRAM STARTED IN JUNE 1955, CONTRACTS TOTALING 
$600,000 HAVE BEEN AWARDED FOR WORK TO AID THE HANDICRAFTERS OF 
UNDERDEVELOPED NATIONS. THE PROGRAM IS BEING HANDLED BY THE STATE 
DEPARTMENT'S INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION ADMINISTRATION. 

THE ICA IS WORKING THROUGH INDUSTRIAL DESIGN FIRMS IN AN 
ATTEMPT TO MAKE THE HANDICRAFT PRODUCT OF THESE COUNTRIES EASIER TO 
SELL IN FOREIGN MARKETS. ESPECIALLY THE UNITED STATESe 

A EFFORTS ALREADY HAVE BEEN MADE AT HELPING MAKE BASKETS 
WVOODENWARE, BOWLS AND VARIOUS BAMBOO ARTICLES MORE MARKETABLE. 

UNUSUALLY, IT WAS THE HOOVER COMMISSION, AN IMPORTANT VOICE 
IN THE CLAMOR FOR ECONOMY IN GOVERNMENT, THAT GAVE THE PROJECT ITS 
BIGGEST BOOST, ACCORDING TO THE HEAD OF "A MAJOR PRIVATE FIRM IN 

DESIGN RESEARCH, INCs, HAS BEEN ACTIVE IN THE INTERNATIONAL 
PROJECT SINCE ITS INCEPTION. PARKISTAN, SURINAM AND OTHER NATIONS 
HAVE BEEN SURVEYED BY THE CHICAGO FIRM UNDER U.S. GOVERNMENT 
SPONSORSHIP. 

OROUAVE, CHAPMAN, 48) HEAD OF DESIGN RESEARCH, EXPLAINED THE 

"PRIMARILY, WE'RE TRYING TO REACH THE BASIC CULTURE IN THESE 
COUNTRIES, X % X TO TEACH THESE PEOPLE HOV TO PRODUCE GOODS THEY 
CAN SELL AND STEP UP THEIR OUTPUTs® 

THE PROJECT IS PROVIDING HELP AT THE GRASS ROOTS -- ORy MORE 
COMMONLY, -- GRASS HUTS LEVEL FOR SOME OF THE WORLD'S OLDEST 
SIMPLEST AND MOST BASIC CRAFTS. THE STEP-BY-STEP OPERATION BY DESIGN 
RESEARCH, INC.e, IN A SUBJECT COUNTRY USUALLY COVERS THESE STEPS: 

AFTER THE NATION REQUESTS HELP AND THIS COUNTRY ACREFS TO 
SUPPLY IT DESIGNERS ARE SENT TO MAKE THE STUDY. 

THE DESIGNERS TREK INTO OBSCURE VILLAGES AND EXAMINE THE RAW 
MATERIALS AVAILABLE AND WHAT THE NATIVES ARE CAPABLE OF DOING WITH 
THEM. THEY FILL NOTEBOOKS ON HOW THE NATIVES CARVE, WEAVE AND 

SAMPLES AND SKETCHES ARE RETURNED TO THE U.S. FOR FURTHER 
STUDY.» WITH THE DATA ASSEMBLED, THE DESIGNERS TRY TO COME UP WITH 
IDEAS THAT WILL INCREASE THE APPEAL OF NATIVE PRODUCTS FOR POTENTIAL 

ESSENTIALLY, A DESIGN RESEARCH, INC., SPOKESMAN SAID. TH 
TRAVELING DESIGNERS ARE TRYING TO’REDUCE THE WIDE CULTURAL 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE MACHINE-POWERED, MASS PRODUCTION SYSTEMS oF 
THE UNITED STATES AND OTHER INDUSTRIALIZED NATIONS AND UNDER- 
DEVELOPED AGRICULTURAL COUNTRIES. 

BESIDES PAKISTAN AND SURINAM, 17 NATIONS HAVE BEEN VISITED 
SO FAR UNDER THE ICA PROJECT. ‘THEY ARE GREECE, TURKEY, JORDAN 
LEPANON, KOREA, ISRAEL) TURKEY, FORMOSA, AFGHANISTAN, MEXICO 
SALVADOR, JAMAICA, COSTA RICA, THAILAND) VIET NAM, CAMBODIA AN

J AERIAL REFUELING SYSTEM THAT ASSERTEDLY INCREASES THE 
STRIKING RANGE OF JET FIGHTER-BOMBERS "BY UP TO 70 PER CENT.® 

BASICALLY, THE SYSTEM CONVERTS AN ORDINARY JET FIGHTER PLANE INTO 
\ TANKERe A “BUDDY TANK" WITH A FUEL CAPACITY OF 450 GALLONS IS 
ATTACHED TO THE UNDER-WING PYLON OF THE JET FIGHTER. THE TANK IS 
SEPARATED INTO TWO COMPARTMENTS, ONE CONTAINING FUEL AND THE OTHER THI 
REFUELING MECHANISM. 

WHEN A FAST FLYING FIGHTER PLANE NEEDS FUEL, IT APPROACHES THE 
"BUDDY" PLANE WHICH LOWERS THE REFUELING MECHANISM. WITHOUT REDUCING 
ITS SPEED, THE THIRSTY FIGHTER INSERTS A “PROBE” THAT EXTENDS FROM 
THE FORWARD EDGE OF ITS WING INTO A "DROGUE” OR FUNNEL SHAPED 
SPOUT AT THE END OF THE REFUELING MECHANISM. 

FUEL IS TRANSFERRED QUICKLY FROM THE "BUDDY" PLANE TO THE FIGHTER 
JHILE BOTHER CONTINUE AT FULL SPEED. THE FIGHTER DOES NOT HAVE TO 


5LOV ead AS IN CONVENTIONAL REFUELING.

BY ENABLING FIGHTERS TO DOUBLE AS TANKERS, THE SYSTEM 
SERMITS A TACTICAL UNIT TO BECOME SELF-SUFFICIENT AND MORE VERSATILE, 
THE COMPANY STATES, SINCE THE SAME PLANE WHICH CARRIES THE BOMB ON 
INE MISSION CAN BE A TANKER ON THE NEXT. 

THE SYSTEM WILL UNDERGO EVALUATION BY THE AIR NATIONAL GUARD. IT 
JAS DEVELOPED BY REPUBLIC WORKING WITH SCHULZ TOOL CO. AND THE AIR

SHE SAILED TO RANGOON TO PICK UP CARGO FOR ISRAELS ae 


THE SHIP IS CARRYING 3,357 TONS OF BURMA RICE AND 15 CASES OF 
GENERAL CARGO FROM RANGOON TO THE ISRAELI MEDITERRANEAN PORT OF HAIFA. 
SINCE THE 1948 PALESTINE WAR, EGYPT HAS BARRED ISRAELI SHIPS FROM 
THE CANAL AND HAS SOUGHT AT TIMES TO BAR CARGO BOUND TO OR FROM ISRAEL 
IN FOREIGN SHIPS. EGYPT CLAIMS THE RIGHT BECAUSE A STATE OF WAR 
STILL EXISTS BETWEEN IT AND ISRAEL AND SAYS SECURITY IS INVOLVED. 

THE DANISH SHIP WILL PROCEED THROUGH THE NATIONALIZED WATERWAY IN A 
NORTHBOUND CONVOY, PERHAPS TOMORROW, EGYPTIAN AUTHORITIFS SAID. THE 
2,355-TON FREIGHTER MISSED THIS MORNING'S NORTHBOUND CONVOY AND HAS 
TO WAIT UNTIL TOMORROW'S GROUP OF SHIPS IS SHEPHERDED THROUGH. 

OFFICIALS MAINTAINED THE SHIP IS BEING GIVEN THE SAME TREATMENT AS 
ANY OTHER TRANSITING THE CANAL. - 

NORMAL PROCEDURE, AN OFFICIAL SAID, IS TO PERMIT LIMITED CARBO, / 
THROUGH TO ISRAEL IF IT IS ADDRESSED tO INDIVIDUAL IMPORTERS AND~ é 
IS CARRIED BY A NON-ISRAELI SHIP. IF IT IS ADDRESSED TO THE ISRAELI 
GOVERNMENT OR ITS MILITARY FORCES, THE CARGO MAY BE CONFISCATED, THE 
OFFICIAL SAID. 

THE SAILOR IN CUSTODY, RAFI EILON, WAS FIRST CONFINED TO HIS 
CABIN WITH AN EGYPTIAN GUARD POSTED AT HIS DOOR, CANAL AUTHORITIES 
SAIDe THEY DID NOT SAY WHEN THE TOFT STOPPED AT EILAT. 

THE TOFT'S CAPTAIN, HANS LOLK, TOLD OFFICIALS MOST OF THE 
SHIP'S PAPERS WERE LOST IN A SHIPBOARD FIRE JUNE 29.

7AMORSKY, FROM MOLINE, ILLe, WENT TO INDONESIA THREE YEARS ACO 
AS A FORD FOUNDATION LINGUISTIC RESEARCH SCHOLAR. HIS WIFE IS IN 
MOLINE. HIS FATHER IS IN CHICAGO. 

HE SAID HE WAS ARRESTED BY MILITARY POLICE MAY 18 ON THE ISLAND OF 
HALMAHERA. HIS BEACH HOUSE WAS SURROUNDED BY ABOUT 20 ARMED MILITARY 
MEN. THE DOORS WERE BLOCKED AND HE WAS TOLD HE WAS UNDER ARREST. 

WHEN ZAMORSKY ASKED MILITARY OFFICIALS THE REASON FOR HIS ARREST 
THEY SAID THEY DID NOT KNOW. THEY TOLD HIM THEY RECEIVED ORDERS 
FROM MILITARY HEADQUARTERS. 

"FOR TWO HOURS THEY SEARCHED MY HOUSE AND IT LOOKED LIKE THEY 
WANTED EITHER SOME DOCUMENTS OR A TRACE OF STORAGE OF ARMS WHICH I WAS 
SUPPOSED TO SUPPLY TO REBELS," HE SAID. 

HE WAS KEPT UNDER STRICT GUARD BY FIVE ARMED SOLDIERS AT NIGHT AND. 
FOUR DURING THE DAY TIME. HE SAID HE WAS HELD ALONG WITH REBEL 10-9 
PRISONERS. THE REBELS WERE POLITE AND OFFERED CIGARETTES. rey 

ZAMORSKY SAID AN ATTEMPT WAS MADE TO KIDNAP HIM BEFORE AND AFTER 
DETENTION, BUT HE WAS LUCKY TO ESCAPE. HE DID NOT GO INTO DETAILS. 

HE SAID THAT DURING HIS DETENTION HE WAS ASKED ABOUT *CERTAIN 
DOCUMENTS WHICH WOULD HAVE COMMITTED ME TO THINGS WHICH I WAS NOT 
RESPO ‘ .

"I THINK THE PUBLIC IS ENTITLED AT LEAST TO SOME OF THE

WHEN THE JAPANESE HIT PEARL HARBOR, COL. LINDBERGH FOUND IT 
IMPOSSIBLE BECAUSE OF THE POLITICAL CLIMATE TO PARTICIPATE IN THE WAR 
AS A MEMBER OF THE ARMED FORCES, 

"SO HE WENT TO WAR AS A TECHNICAL REPRESENTATIVE OF THE AIRCRAFT

"ALL THE PERTINENT FACTS ARE ON THE RECORD, BUT THAT CLOSELY 
GUARDED GOVERNMENT RECORD IS UNAVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC. LET ME PUSH

HAD FLOWN COMBAT MISSIONS, AND HAD SHOT DOWN A JAPANESE FIGHTER, BUT 
WEDEMEYER GAVE MORE DETAILS TODAY, 

LINDBERGH WAS COMMISSIONED A BRIGADIER GENERAL IN THE AIR FORCE 
RESERVE IN 1954 ON NOMINATION BY GEN. EISENHOWER AND NOW IS A 
CONSULTANT FOR PAN-AMERICAN WORLD AIRWAYS.

PERFORMANCES UNDER COMBAT CONDITIONS WITH A VIEW TOWARD IMPROVING

LONDON, JULY 25 CAP)-THE UNITED STATES PROPOSED TODAY THAT DURING THE 


FI NT A SCIENTIFIC COMMITTEE SHOULD WORK OUT A 
WAY FOR DEVOTING ALL OUTER SPACE MISSILE RESEARCH TO PEACEFUL PURPOSES. 
HAROLD Es STASSEN TOLD THE UNITED NATIONS DISARMAMENT SUBCOMMITTEE 

RUSSIA AND THE WEST SHOULD JOIN FORCES TO FIND A WAY OF CONTROLLING 
ALL OBJECTS SENT INTO OUTER SPACE. HE SAID THE FIRST STAGE OF ANY 
DISARMAMENT TREATY SHOULD INCLUDE A FIRM COMMITMENT BY ALL SIGNATORY 
NATIONS THAT SUCH A COMMITTEE WOULD BE CREATED, _ 

THE ACTUAL BANNING OF SUCH RESEARCH, HOWEVER, WOULD NOT COME UNTIL 
THE SECOND STAGE OF DISARMAMENT--OR UNTIL AFTER SCIENTISTS HAD AGREED 
ON A SYSTEM OF ENFORCEMENT. 

TODAY'S PROPOSAL APPEARED TO MAKE A MUCH MORE CAUTIOUS APPROACH, 
ir NOT AN OUTRIGHT CHANGE IN ATTITUDE, ON THE PART OF THE UNITED 
STATES TOWARD THE MISSILE PROBLEM. 

STASSEN PROPOSED ON APRIL 25, IN THE SUBCOMMITTEE’S FIRST 
ROUND OF DISCUSSIONS THAT ALL RESEARCH ON INTERCONTINENTAL

CONSULTATIONS BETWEEN THE UNITED STATES AND OTHER WESTERN NATIONS.

HOWEVER, IT APPEARED THAT MISSILES MAY PRESENT A MAJOR STICKING POINT 
FOR EAST-WEST AGREEMENT.

OF THE EARTH’S ATMOSPHERE.. |

CONTROLS SET UP FOR CONVENTIONAL WEAPONS. THE RUSSIANS HAVE 
PROPOSED IN THE PAST THAT SHORTER RANGE AND INTERMEDIATE MISSILES --

WHEN THE CONFLICT BETWEEN SAUD AND THE BRITISH AROSE OVER 
BURAIMI OASIS, ARAMCO QUIETLY AGREED NOT TO MAKE ANY CLAIM 
ON BURAIMI AS’PART OF ITS CONCESSION AREA SO THE OIL QUESTION WOULD 
NOT ENTER THE ARGUMENT. 

AT THE TIME OF THE BURAIMI CRISIS, SAUD SAID HE WOULD OFFER THE 
BURAIMI CONCESSION TO A BRITISH COMPANY IF HIS SOVEREIGNTY OVER 
THE OASIS IS ESTABLISHED. THE AREA NORMALLY WOULD HAVE BEEN IN 
ARAMCO TERRITORY. ARAMCO CONCURRED IN SAUD'S DECISION. 

ARAMCO HOLDS MOST OF THE EASTERN HALF OF SAUDI ARABIA AS ITS 
CONCESSION BUT HAS NO CONCESSION IN THE WESTERN HALF. ARAMCO'S 
CONCESSION RUNS ALONG THE PERSIAN GULF TO THE BOUNDARY OF THE SERIES 
BRITISH PROTECTORATES KNOWN AS TRUCIAL OMAN. IT FANS OUT SOUTHWARD 
ACROSS THE LITTLE KNOWN "EMPTY QUARTER” OF SAUDI ARABIA. 

AT SOME UNDEFINED POINT ON THE SOUTHERN FRINGE OF THIS EMPTY 
QUARTER SAUDI ARABIA MERGES WITH OMAN. BOUNDARIES IN THE REGION 
HAVE NEVER BEEN CLEARLY DEFINED. THE BRITISH PETROLEUM CO. HAS A 
CONCESSION IN OMAN BUT EXPLORATION SO FAR HAS BEEN UNSUCCESSFUL. 

TALK OF BRITISH-AMERICAN COMPETITION FOR OIL HAS GIVEN EGYPT'S 
CONTROLLED PRESS A GOLDEN OPPORTUNITY TO PORTRAY BRITISH INTERVENTION 
IN OMAN AS PART OF A STRUGGLE BETWEEN TWO OIL THIRSTY NATIONS.

; 7 (AP)-SEN. JAVITS (R-NY) SAID TODAY THE 
STATE DEPART SUGGESTION TO BROADEN THE LONDON 
DISARMAMENT TALKS TO INCLUDE EFFORTS TO STRENGTHEN UNITED NATIONS PEACE 

HE MADE PUBLIC AN EXCHANGE OF CORRESPONDENCE WHICH HE SAID DEMON- 
STRATES THIS GOVERNMENT'S DETERMINATION TO KEEP THE CONCENTRATION AT 
LONDON ON SEEKING "A FIRST-STEP DISARMAMENT AGREEMENT WITH THE SOVIET 

"EVEN THOUGH I HAVE ADVOCATED THE POSSIBILITY OF INCLUDING IN THE 
NEGOTIATIONS SOME NEW EFFORTS TO IMPROVE THE PEACE MAINTENANCE MACHINERY 
OF THE UN, AND BELIEVE THIS TO BE SOUND," HE SAID, "I CAN UNDERSTAND THE 
POSITION OF THE DEPARTMENT OF STATE IN WISHING TO MAINTAIN THE 
DISCUSSIONS ON THE PRESENT STATUS." 

PRESIDENT EISENHOWER TODAY ORDERED SECRETARY OF STATE DULLES TO FLY 
TO LONDON TOMORROW. IT WAS REPORTED THE SECRETARY WOULD DETERMINE 
WHETHER THE TALKS SHOULD CONTINUE OR BE STOPPED. 

JAVITS SAID HE COMMENDED THE DEPARTMENT FOR "ITS EXPRESSED DETERMINA- 
TION TO ACHIEVE A WORKABLE DISARMAMENT PROGRAM PROTECTED BY INSPECTION 
AND CONTROL," BUT ADDED: 

"THE POSITION TAKEN BY THE U.S. TO MAKE THE U.N. PEACE MAINTENANCE 
MACHINERY MORE EFFECTIVE NEEDS TO BE PURSUED WITH DETERMINATION. 

"ALTHOUGH THIS SUBJECT APPARENTLY WILL NOT BE INCLUDED IN THE 
PRESENT LONDON NEGOTIATIONS, IT SHOULD BE PURSUED CURRENTLY IN THE 
UsNe AND WITH ITS MEMBERS." 

JAVITS WROTE SECRETARY OF STATE DULLES JULY 2 THE SUBSTANCE OF A 
FOREIGN POLICY SPEECH THE SENATOR MADE AT A COLGATE UNIVERSITY CONFER- 
ENCE AT HAMILTON, N&lt;Ye, THE DAY BEFORE, SUGGESTING DISCUSSIONS AT 
LONDON OF A PERMANENT UN PEACE FORCE AND OTHER STEPS BY THE UN. 

HIS REPLY CAME JULY 18 FROM JOHN S. HOCHLAND II, ACTING ASSISTANT 
SECRETARY FOR CONGRESSIONAL RELATIONS. HE SAID THE STATE DEPARTMENT 


"HAS SERIOUS DOUBTS ABOUT THE WISDOM AND PRACTICABILITY OF INTRODUCING 
NEV ELEMENTS" INTO AN ALREADY FORMIDABLE AND COMPLICATED TASK." 

HE SAID IT WAS HOPED THE FIVE-POWER NEGOTIATORS "MAY BE ABLE TO 
REACH A FIRST PHASE AGREEMENT WHICH WOULD HAVE THE EFFECT OF BRINGING 
ABOUT A REDUCTION AND CONTROL OF THE ARMAMENTS AND ARMED FORCES OF THESE 
COUNTRIES" ~-THE UNITED STATES, CANADA, FRANCE, BRITAIN AND SOVIET 
RUSSIA. 

THESE ARE THE FIVE NATIONS REPRESENTED AT THE LONDON CONFERENCE. 

THE "MAIN TASK® FOR THE PRESENT, HE SAID, IS THE ACHIEVEMENT OF A 
FIRST PHASE AGREEMENT WHICH, "IF EFFECTIVELY IMPLEMENTED COULD SERVE 
TO REDUCE TENSIONS."

ANGUISHED CRIES IN BONN TODAY BUT NO FLAT DENIAL, 

THE DEFENSE MINISTRY, SIDESTEPPING CONFIRMATION OR DENIAL OF THE 
REPORTS. SAID ONLY THAT BRITAIN AND WEST GERMANY WERE ENGACED IN AN 
SEXCHANCE OF INFORMATION® ON WEAPON RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT. 

OTHER SOURCES IN A POSITION TO KNOW SAID IT WAS NO SECRET THAT 
LONDON AND BONN WERE MOVING TOWARD A JOINT RESEARCH PROGRAM WHICH 
MIGHT EVENTUALLY LEAD TO JOINT PRODUCTION OF CERTAIN WEAPONS. 

EXACTLY WHICH WEAPONS WAS SOMETHING NO ONE HERE WOULD SAY. 

IN LONDON, INFORMED SOURCES SAID THE TWO COUNTRIES WERE TALKING 
ABOUT GUIBED MISSILES, LONG-RANGE ROCKETS, A SECRET NEW AUTOMATIC 
RIFLE AND OTHER TYPES OF EQUIPMENT. 

ASKED FOR COMMENT, THE DEFENSE MINISTRY SAID THE REPORT ABOUT 
A NEW SECRET AUTOMATIC RIFLE WAS UNTRUE, BUT IT SAID NOTHING ABOUT 
THE GUIDED MISSILES AND LONG-RANGE ROCKETS.» 

IT WAS CLEAR THAT THE LONDON REPORTS WERE DISTURBING TO THE WEST 
CERMAN GOVERNMENT, PARTICULARLY WITH CHANCELLOR KONRAD ADENAUER 
FNCAGED IN A BITTER ELECTION BATTLE. 

THE REPORTS WERE SET IN MOTION BY A MEETING SCHEDULED IN LONDON 
MONDAY BETWEEN WEST GERMAN AND BRITISH DEFENSE EXPERTS. A JOINT 
COMMITTEE WAS SET UP RECENTLY AFTER TALKS BETWEEN DEFENSE MINISTERS 
OF THE TWO COUNTRIES. 

THE BONN DEFENSE MINISTRY SAID THE TALKS WERE TO BE BASED ON AN 
EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION. OTHER BONN SOURCES SAID ONE OF THE KEY 
ASPECTS OF THE TALKS WAS THE QUESTION OF JOINT RESEARCH. ALSO 
INVOLVED IN THE DISCUSSION WAS A QUESTION OF WHETHER BRITAIN WAS GOING 
TO SUPPLY THE WEST CERMAN ARMY WITH CERTAIN WEAPONS AND OTHER 
MILITARY MATERIALS.

STATES, "AS A MEANS TO LESSEN INTERNATIONAL TENSION AND STRENGTHEN 
MUTUAL UNDERSTANDING AND COOPERATION AMONG PEOPLES.” 

*SINCE THE EXCHANGE OF RADIO AND TELEVISION BROADCASTS BETWEEN THE 
SOVIET UNION AND THE UNITED STATES COULD FACILITATE THE ACHIEVEMENT 
OF THESE NOBLE AIMS, THE SOVIET GOVERNMENT IS READY TO STUDY THE 
(AMERICAN) PROPOSAL ON A BASIS OF MUTUAL EQUALITY," IT SAID. 

HOWEVER, THE NOTE SAID, "IT WOULD BE ONLY PROPER TO EXAMINE THIS 
QUESTION TOGETHER WITH OTHER QUESTIONS PERTAINING TO THE DEVELOPMENT 
OF CONTACTS BETWEEN THE SOVIET UNION AND THE UNITED STATES, INCLUDING 
THE ELIMINATION OF ARTIFICIAL BARRIERS ESTABLISHED BY THE AMERICAN 
SIDE WHICH INTERFERE WITH THE DEVELOPMENT OF ALL=ROUND RELATIONS

NATION" BECAUSE THEY INTERFERE WITH THE COUNTRY’S INTERNAL SECUR 

THAT JENNER SAID, IS WHY HE HAS INTRODUCED LEGISLATION To STRIE" 
THE COURT OF THE RIGHT TO HEAR APPEALS OF CASES INVOLVING STATE op 
FEDERAL CHARGES OF SUBVERSION, OR CONTEMPT OF CONGRESS. 

IN A RADIO-TV INTERVIEW (NBC-MEET THE PRESS), JENNER SAID HE 
DOESN'T WANT TO "CURB OR HANDICAP THE COURT." HOWEVER, HE SAID, THE 
HIGH COURT HAS GONE "RAMPANT® AND HAS ®"DONE MORE TO HELP THE COMMUNIST 
CAUSE IN THIS NATION THAN ANYTHING THAT HAS RAPPENED IN THE LAST 


QUARTER OF A CENTURY." 
HIS BILL, JENNER SAID, IS AIMED AT LETTING THE STATES PROTECT THEIR 
INTERNAL SECURITY, KEEPING FBI FILES FROM "BEING VIOLATED" AND 
PERMITTING CONGRESSIONAL COMMITTEES "TO GO AHEAD AND BO THEIR WoORK.® 
THE BILL, HE SAID, WOULD DEAL ONLY WITH MATTERS AFFECTING THE INTER- 
NAL SECURITY OF THE UNITED STATES. 
JENNER SAID THE SUPREME COURT "HAS GONE FAR BEYOND ITS JURISDICTION® 
AND INSTEAD OF MERELY INTERPRETI G THE CONSTITUTION IS MAKING LAW.

"THE REBELS HAVE NOW BEEN ENCLOSED IN A SMALL BUT DIFFICULT 
MOUNTAIN AREA, FORCES NOW SURROUNDING THEM ARE REDUCING THE AREA THAT 
THE REBELS HOLD AND ARE MAKING THEIR POSITION MORE DIFFICULT.” 

THE REBELS HOLD AN AREA ROUGHLY 25 BY 15 MILES AND IT HAS 
BEEN DESCRIBED AS ALMOST ENTIRELY RUGGED MOUNTAINS. 

THE REBELS, LED BY IMAM GHALEB BIN ALI, WHO RECENTLY RETURNED 
FROM SAUDI ARABIA, BEGAN THE REVOLT 11 DAYS AGO IN AN ATTEMPT TO SET 
UP AN INDEPENDENT SULTANATE IN OMAN. BRITISH OFFICIALS AND THE ‘SULTAN 
HAVE ACCUSED SAUDI ARABIA OF GIVING THE REBELS MODERN MILITARY WEAPONS. 

BRITISH PLANES CONTINUED TO DROP LEAFLETS OVER THE REBEL-HELD AREA 
CALLING ON THE TRIBES TO TURN OUT TRAITORS. 

TODAYS COMMUNIQUE WAS THE FIRST OFFICIAL INDICATIONS THAT THE 
SULTAN’ S FORCES HAVE TAKEN THE OFFENSIVE AGAINST THE REBELS. THESE 
FORCES WERE DEFEATED ON THE OPENING DAY OF THE REVOLT AND FORCED TO 
WITHDRAW. 

THE CHIEF BRITISH POLITICAL OFFICER FOR THE PERSIAN GULF ARWAYSALD 
EARLIER THE REBELS MAD LOST THEIR MOMENTUM AND WERE BOTTLED UP!

CONDON. JULY 29 CAF REIGN SECRETARY SELWYN LLOYD SAID TODAY HE 
WOULD DISCUSS THE REBELLION IN OMAN WITH JOHN FOSTER DULLES DURING THE 
UeSe SECRETARY OF STATE*’S VISIT TO LONDON. DULLES ARRIVES TONIGHT. 

LLOYD SAID IN A HOUSE OF COMMONS STATEMENT THAT THIS COUNTRY STEPPED 
INTO THE OMAN TRIBAL REBELLION NOT ONLY TO HELP THE PRO-BRITISH 
SULTAN OF MUSCAT AND OMAN BUT ALSO TO PROTECT HER OWN VAST INTERESTS 
IN THE OIL-RICH PERSIAN GULF AREA. 

HE HAS NO DOUBT, HE SAID, THAT THE MATTER WILL COME UP DURING 
HIS DISCUSSIONS WITH DULLES. 

AT PRESIDENT EISENHOWER*S PERSONAL REQUEST, DULLES IS FLYING TO 
LONDON TO TAKE A HAND IN THE EAST-WEST DISARMAMENT NEGOTIATIONS.

DETERMINED AT ONCE.

TODAY THE NAZIS OFFERED IN 1940 TO PUT THE DUKE OF WINDSOR BACK ON 

THE BRITISH THRONE PROVIDED HE UNDERCUT PRIME MINISTER CHURCHILL AND 

GOT HIS PEOPLE TO SURRENDER. 

WINDSOR REFUSED DESPITE PHONY BOMB SCARES AND OTHER °THREATS® 
TO HIS LIFE AND THE LIFE OF THE AMERICAN-BORN DUCHESS--°THE WOMAN I 
LOVE® FOR WHOM HE GAVE UP THE THRONE IN 1936. 

BUT THE NAZIS THOUGHT HE “HESITATED EVEN UP TO THE LAST MOMENT.® 
THEY BLAMED THE DUKE’S LEGAL ADVISER AND THEN DEPUTY FOREIGN MINISTER, 
SIR WALTER MONCKTON. AS THE NEMESIS WHO "INFLUENCED" WINDSOR TO 
REJECT THEIR GRANDIOSE PLAN. 

THERE WAS NOTHING IN THE DOCUMENTS ABOUT ANY DIRECT CONTACT BETWEEN 
THE DUKE AND ANY GERMANS. APPARENTLY, THE GERMANS CARRIED ON ALL 
THEIR EFFORTS THROUGH PORTUGUESE AND SPANISH INTERMEDIARIES. 

THE BRITISH EMBASSY, COMMENTING ON THE DOCUMENTS, DECLARED THEY 
PARE NECESSARILY A MUCH TAINTED SOURCE." 

THE EMBASSY ADDED: 

®THE DUKE WAS SUBJECT TO HEAVY PRESSURE FROM MANY QUARTERS TO 
STAY IN EUROPE. WHERE THE GERMANS HOPED THAT HE WOULD EXERT HIS 
INFLUENCE AGAINST THE POLICIES OF HIS MAJESTY’S GOVERNMENT. 

®HIS ROYAL HIGHNESS (THE DUKE) NEVER WAVERED IN HIS LOYALTY TO THE 
BRITISH CAUSE OR IN HIS DETERMINATION TO TAKE UP HIS OFFICIAL POST 
AS GOVERNOR OF THE BAHAMAS ON THE DATE AGREED « « «

THEY FAILED TO DO ITe®
